jobs.description:
Employment Type: Full-time
Work Location: Remote - PHILIPPINES

Compensation: With flexibility based on certification, multi-country payroll experience, technical expertise, and overall qualifications.

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

Due to continued growth, we are seeking a highly experienced Senior Payroll Specialist with high-level payroll expertise to lead end-to-end payroll for our growing workforce.

This is a senior role for a payroll expert with deep, hands-on experience who can own accurate, on-time, compliant payroll across multiple pay groups and, where applicable, multiple countries. We are particularly interested in CPP-, FPC-, or equivalently certified professionals, but we will also consider highly accomplished non-certified payroll leads with directly relevant high-volume or multi-entity experience.

The position is fully remote and works closely with HR, Finance, and Recruitment as the go-to expert for payroll questions, audits, and process improvement.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Manage and process full-cycle payroll for all employees and pay groups, ensuring accuracy and on-time delivery every cycle.
  • Calculate and validate wages, overtime, allowances, bonuses, commissions, deductions, and final pay.
  • Administer statutory deductions, government contributions, and tax withholdings, and file remittances by required deadlines.
  • Reconcile payroll registers, general ledger entries, and bank transfers with Finance each cycle.
  • Maintain and audit employee payroll data, including new hires, terminations, salary changes, and leave balances.
  • Review timekeeping and attendance data and resolve discrepancies before processing.
  • Prepare payroll reports, year-end tax documents, and data for internal and external audits.
  • Serve as the subject-matter expert on payroll policy, labor regulations, and compliance requirements.
  • Answer employee and manager payroll inquiries professionally and resolve issues promptly.
  • Identify and implement process improvements, controls, and automation within payroll and HRIS systems.
  • Lead, coach, and review the work of payroll staff, and act as the final escalation point for payroll issues.
  • Maintain confidentiality of all employee compensation and personal data.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8+ years of progressive payroll experience, including at least 3–5 years in a senior or lead payroll role.
  • CPP (Certified Payroll Professional), FPC (Fundamental Payroll Certification), or equivalent credential strongly preferred.
  • Highly experienced non-certified payroll professionals with a proven senior-level track record are encouraged to apply.
  • Expert-level knowledge of payroll tax, statutory contributions, and labor regulations in [country/countries].
  • Proven ability to independently resolve complex payroll issues, audits, and compliance matters without supervision.
  • Proficiency with payroll and HRIS platforms (e.g., ADP, Paylocity, Workday, or similar) and advanced Excel.
  • Exceptional accuracy, attention to detail, and analytical skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Commitment to confidentiality, integrity, and compliant, high-quality work.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills.
  • Reliable internet connection and a secure, quiet home workspace.
  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

  • Multi-state or multi-country payroll (e.g., Philippines, Singapore, UAE, US).
  • Payroll for staffing, recruitment, or high-volume hourly workforces.
  • Payroll system implementation, migration, or automation projects.
  • Year-end processing, payroll audits, and statutory reporting.
  • Benefits, leave, and timekeeping administration.
  • Working with outsourced payroll providers or employer-of-record partners.

WHY JOIN US?

  • Join a growing business that is investing in its people and operations.
  • Work fully remote while owning a high-impact function every employee relies on.
  • Shape payroll processes, controls, and systems as the company scales.
  • Receive competitive compensation based on your credentials and experience, with flexibility above the typical hiring range for exceptional qualifications.
  • Build a long-term career with a team that values accuracy, integrity, and continuous learning.

We are an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to legally protected characteristics.

Discover your 100% YOU with MicroSourcing!

Position: Ad Operations Coach

Work setup: Work from home

Why join MicroSourcing?

You'll have:

  • Competitive Rewards: Enjoy above-market compensation, healthcare coverage on day one, plus one or more dependents, paid time-off with cash conversion, group life insurance, and performance bonuses

  • A Collaborative Spirit: Contribute to a positive and engaging work environment by participating in company-sponsored events and activities.

  • Career Growth: Take advantage of opportunities for continuous learning and career advancement.

  • Inclusive Teamwork: Be part of a team that celebrates diversity and fosters an inclusive culture.

Key Responsibilities

The Ad Operations Coach is an individual-contributor role responsible for preparing new and existing employees to perform accurate, efficient, and compliant digital advertising operations. The specialist delivers new-hire, refresher, remedial, and cross-training; assists with client-specific and platform-specific training; and partners with subject matter experts and team leads to translate operational processes into structured learning.

The role requires at least two years of hands-on Ad Operations experience and demonstrated experience implementing or delivering structured training, which may have been gained in another professional discipline. The specialist develops training materials, evaluates production readiness, supports employees during nesting and early production, conducts skill set reviews, and may coordinate with clients or external partners when required.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Training Delivery and Facilitation

  • Deliver new-hire, refresher, remedial, and cross-training for Ad Operations employees in classroom and virtual environments.

  • Assist with client-specific and platform-specific training in partnership with subject matter experts and team leads, including practical exercises and campaign simulations.

  • Adapt training pace and approach to learner needs while reinforcing accuracy, quality assurance, information security, and process compliance.

  • Curriculum and Documentation

  • Creating training materials, practical exercises, assessments, SOPs, job aids, or educational content.

  • Translate workflows, platform procedures, and client requirements into clear, accurate, and standardized training content.

  • Maintain version control and training records and incorporate approved process, platform, and policy changes into learning materials.

  • Assessment, Readiness, and Skill Set Reviews

  • Administer knowledge checks and practical evaluations, document results, and provide timely, actionable feedback to trainees and stakeholders.

  • Assess production readiness and recommend advancement to production, additional coaching, or remediation based on demonstrated knowledge, accuracy, and independent performance.

  • Conduct skill set reviews for existing employees, identify capability gaps, and support targeted development and cross-training plans.

  • Post-Training Support and Collaboration

  • Support nesting and early production through observation, coaching, and coordination with team leads, quality assurance personnel, and operational subject matter experts.

  • Track training outcomes and recurring performance or error trends and use findings to improve curriculum and targeted learning interventions.

  • Collaborate primarily with internal stakeholders and, when required, clients or external partners; communicate learner progress, risks, and training needs clearly and professionally.

Qualifications and Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in any field from an accredited institution is required.

  • A minimum of two years of hands-on Ad Operations experience is required, including experience with campaign setup or trafficking, quality assurance, monitoring, reporting, optimization, or related campaign-management activities.

  • Demonstrated experience implementing or delivering structured training, onboarding, coaching, or formal knowledge transfer is required; this experience may be in Ad Operations or another professional discipline.

  • Hands-on experience with at least one of the following platforms, or a directly comparable advertising platform, is required: Google Ad Manager, Campaign Manager 360, Display & Video 360, FreeWheel, The Trade Desk, Google Ads, Search Ads 360, Meta Ads Manager, TikTok Ads Manager, or Operative.

  • Intermediate or higher proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including formulas, sorting, filtering, formatting, structured data, and spreadsheet-based reporting, with the capacity to learn more advanced functionality quickly.

  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, and Teams.

  • Strong written and verbal English communication, presentation, facilitation, and interpersonal skills.

  • Exceptional attention to detail, sound judgment, strong organization and time management, and the ability to assess performance, deliver constructive feedback, manage multiple training priorities, and adapt to changing operational requirements.

Preferred Experience and Knowledge:

  • Experience supporting nesting, production-readiness decisions, remedial coaching, skill matrices, or structured skill set reviews.

  • Experience across multiple digital advertising channels or platforms, as well as coordination with clients, external partners, or operational subject matter experts.

jobs.description:
Role Title: Principal Engineer / Professor — Technical Expert

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote

Opportunity Snapshot

Pay:$80- $185/hour

Commitment: Flexible — fits alongside your current role

Location: Fully remote

You’ll need: Master’s or PhD in an engineering or physical science field, plus principal-level industry experience or a faculty appointment

Your tasks: Build challenging technical problems from your own domain and define what makes an answer correct

micro1 is engaging principal-level engineers, scientists, and faculty to design the technical problems that measure what AI systems can actually do. Your domain expertise is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.

We’re building this across four areas: aerospace, semiconductors, manufacturing and industrial engineering, and materials science. If your work sits in one of those — or across two of them — this is for you.

The work draws on what you already know: the problems where the textbook answer isn’t enough, where the right approach depends on reading the constraints correctly, where a plausible-looking solution is quietly wrong.

What you’ll do

  1. Design difficult technical problems from your own area, with realistic constraints and supporting data.
  2. Provide the correct solution and walk through the reasoning that gets there.
  3. Define objective criteria for correctness, so another expert reviewing the work would reach the same verdict.
  4. Review problems built by other contributors for technical accuracy and soundness of method.
  5. Flag problems that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable rather than submitting them.

What we’re looking for

  1. Master’s or PhD in engineering, physics, materials, or a closely related field.
  2. Principal, staff, or fellow-level experience at a major engineering organization, a national lab, or a faculty appointment at a leading university.
  3. Deep technical depth in at least one area, with hands-on ownership of the work.
  4. Able to explain why an answer is correct clearly enough that another expert could verify it.
  5. Publications, patents, or a record of technical leadership is a strong plus.

How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: PhysioNet Competitor (Biomedical Signal Processing & ML)

Pay: $60–$120/hour

Location: Global, fully remote

Job Type: Contractor (~15 hours per week)

Schedule: Flexible-you choose the hours and days you work, including weekends if desired

micro1 is engaging specialists with experience in the PhysioNet Challenge or comparable biomedical signal processing and machine learning competitions. In this role, you will apply your scientific programming, signal processing, and modeling expertise to create, solve, and evaluate advanced technical problems that help improve next-generation AI systems.

We are looking for people who have worked directly with physiological signals and can turn noisy, real-world data into a rigorous and reproducible analysis. Strong candidates will be able to explain the methods they developed, the experiments they ran, the technical decisions they personally owned, and how they validated their results. No prior experience working on AI training projects is required.

Scope of Work

  1. Create technically rigorous, self-contained problems involving biomedical signals, time-series data, signal processing, and machine learning.
  2. Develop clear reference solutions using Python, MATLAB, or another appropriate scientific computing environment.
  3. Work with tasks involving signal preprocessing, filtering, segmentation, feature extraction, representation learning, classification, or forecasting.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Participation in a PhysioNet/Computing in Cardiology Challenge or a comparable biomedical signal processing or scientific machine learning competition.
  2. Strong competition results and evidence of a substantive personal technical contribution.
  3. Public evidence of your work through an official team result, conference paper, technical report, open-source repository, or meaningful code contribution.
  4. Hands-on experience with physiological signals such as ECG, EEG, PPG, EMG, respiratory signals, polysomnography, or other clinical time-series data.

Process

  1. Apply to the role and complete the screening questions.
  2. Complete an AI interview of approximately 30 minutes.
  3. Complete the hiring manager review.

Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based. Experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete each task may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow.

Minimum submission requirements apply.

Start Timeline & Availability

  1. We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts who are ready to begin immediately. If selected, you will be expected to start your first task within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

jobs.description:
Role Title: Game Developer

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote

micro1 is engaging Game Developers to contribute to a pioneering customer project focused on evaluating and advancing AI capabilities in the domain of game creation and interaction. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. Leverage your hands-on experience to build authentic debugging and feature challenges within real game projects, directly impacting how AI agents learn to analyze, play, and develop games. Developers from all backgrounds—whether from AAA studios, indie circles, or solo projects—are encouraged to participate.

Scope of Work

  1. Design and build small-scale game projects or interactive scenes in a major game engine to serve as the foundation for assessment tasks.
  2. Integrate realistic gameplay bugs that require thorough playtesting and on-screen analysis to discover and resolve.
  3. Develop multifaceted gameplay feature challenges that rely on multiple in-game systems and mechanics.
  4. Draft clear and concise briefs for each task, emulating the style of instructions from players, designers, or producers.
  5. Create comprehensive reference solutions—including both bug fixes and feature implementations—for every assignment.
  6. Define detailed success criteria, including input sequences, expected visual outcomes, and verifiable in-game states.
  7. Conduct end-to-end playtesting of each task to guarantee reliability and solvability.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Demonstrated experience in game development, whether in AAA, indie, solo, or serious hobby contexts.
  2. A portfolio or verifiable published work (personal site, itch.io, Steam, GitHub, game jam entries, or shipped title credits). Your portfolio is the most important part of your application and plays a major role in our selection, so please include the work that best represents your skills.
  3. Advanced proficiency with at least one major game engine (Unity, Godot, Unreal), including editor tools, scene management, and debugging utilities.
  4. Comfort with engine scripting languages such as C#, GDScript, C++, or Blueprints, with the ability to interpret, troubleshoot, and enhance gameplay logic.
  5. Proven ability to identify and resolve gameplay issues through iterative playtesting.
  6. Strong written communication skills for drafting precise task instructions and acceptance criteria.
  7. Experience in game QA, technical design, systems design, automated testing, or prior contribution to AI evaluation projects is a plus.

Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply. Experts must submit a minimum of tasks per week.

jobs.excerpt: About UsCommunity Phone is building the best phone for communities in America.
jobs.description:
About Us

Community Phone is building the best phone for communities in America. We are your hair salon’s business phone, how your auto-body shop texts you or gets appointments, your local government agency’s operations line, and your mom’s phone that she sometimes answers on her computer. We have more than 20,000 customers today, and are building the Square of phones.

Our team is ~80 people strong, across 15 countries. We are growing quickly, backed by Y Combinator Accelerator and Y Combinator’s Continuity Fund. We are customer-obsessed to the core. When we had a major network outage, everyone from recruiters to engineers to marketers to customer support agents got on the phone with our customers. Our team exemplifies our purpose. Join us on our mission to make it as easy as possible for communities to communicate.

Your Mission

We’re seeing new and interesting product use cases emerge regularly—and we’re looking for someone to help us understand, weigh, and communicate them clearly. As our first dedicated product marketing hire, you’ll define and own the function from the ground up. Reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll be a key partner to Growth, Product, Sales, and Customer Success.

You’ll own the end-to-end positioning, packaging, and go-to-market success of our core phone product and integrated communications suite. You’ll ensure every feature we ship reaches the right audience, with the right message, through the right channel—and that the story lands.

What You’ll Actually Do

Positioning & Messaging

  • Develop and maintain differentiated positioning for each core use case
  • Deliver two updated personas and a refreshed messaging framework within your first 30 days

Launch & Enablement

  • Run GTM for every new feature or pricing change: define launch tiers, write launch briefs, own the comms calendar
  • Lead one Tier-1 launch per month (features used by >20% of users or tied to upsell motion)

Revenue & Sales Alignment

  • Own product marketing inputs to sales playbooks, user lifecycle, sales training, and CS enablement—reviewed biweekly with Sales and CS

Voice of the Customer

  • Talk to users in our ICPs and grow to understand them deeply
  • Partner with CS and Research to generate one new customer case study per month
  • Conduct win/loss interviews monthly to inform roadmap prioritization and competitive content

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Run a weekly GTM sync with Growth, CS, and Product
  • Provide insights for roadmap planning (next two quarters), especially as they relate to competitive shifts or field learnings that influence prioritization

What We’re Looking For

The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to leadLedgerline, an AI-native accounting roll-up. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

There are roughly 10,000 US and Canadian firms in Ledgerline's target band, and the profession is aging out faster than it can replace itself: 57% of multi-owner US firms have no written succession plan, 44% of solo practitioners expect to retire within five years, and new CPA exam candidates dropped from 42,626 to 28,082 in a single year.   • Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Closeline, an AI-native mortgage origination venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Closeline is building the AI-native infrastructure for mortgage origination, purpose-built for brokers and mid-market IMBs. The agent owns the full loan file lifecycle: reading documents, checking them against investor and agency guidelines, and routing each loan through to a decision, acting rather than waiting on a human, and earning more autonomy as trust builds loan by loan. Customer discovery validates a real, recurring cost problem in this segment: lenders spend thousands of dollars to originate a single loan today, a cost that's climbed roughly 35% over the past three years, with up to 80% of that time spent on manual document review.

The US mortgage market processes roughly 6.5 million loans a year across close to 5,000 lending institutions, an estimated $3.25B in addressable software spend at Closeline's pricing. Brokers and mid-market IMBs alone originate about 5.3 million loans a year, representing a $2.65B segment, our initial target market. At target pricing, firms see an estimated 8 to 10x return on what they're currently paying to originate a loan.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven venture building team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

  • Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception

  • Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding

  • Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one

  • Investor and advisor network across fintech and early-stage capital markets

  • A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight’s cross-functional team as your partner

What You’ll Own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead its execution.

  • Strategy — Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning

  • Customer Development — Lead pilots with underwriters, processors, and operations leads, convert them to paid engagements, and build the go-to-market motion

  • Product — Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback

  • Capital — Lead the seed raise, supported by FutureSight's network and traction

  • Team — Recruit and lead the founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

Co-Founder Profile

  • Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company

  • Demonstrated success in B2B SaaS go-to-market, including sales and customer engagement

  • Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital

  • Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent

  • Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company

  • Direct exposure to mortgage origination and lending operations

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

The successful candidate will collaborate closely with designers, architects, engineers, project managers, and production teams to ensure all drawings meet project specifications, fabrication requirements, quality standards, and deadlines.

COMPANY OVERVIEW

Our client is a design studio specializing in technical design and production drawings for custom wood and metal fabrication.

Their work focuses on bridging the gap between concept and manufacturing by translating ideas, sketches, and specifications into accurate 3D models and clear technical documentation ready for real-world production.

They work closely with carpenters, metal workshops, architects, and designers to ensure every drawing is optimized for fabrication processes, materials, and assembly requirements.

jobs.description:
(This job is only available in german)

Worum es geht

SIMON ist die Außendienst-Plattform für alle, die beim Kunden vor Ort arbeiten. Das reicht von der Pharmareferentin in der Apotheke über den Merchandiser im Lebensmittelmarkt bis zum Techniker im Heizungskeller. SIMON setzt auf die vorhandenen ERP- und CRM-Systeme auf und ist technisch in vier bis sechs Wochen startklar. Seit über zehn Jahren arbeiten anspruchsvolle Außendienstteams im Pharmabereich damit.

Jetzt bringen wir SIMON zu weiteren mittelständischen Herstellern, vor allem im Handel und FMCG sowie im technischen Kundendienst. Dafür suchen wir dich: jemanden, der die richtigen Leute findet, anspricht und vom ersten Kontakt bis zum produktiven Einsatz begleitet.

Wie wir verkaufen

Wir verkaufen SIMON so, wie man einen neuen Kollegen einstellt. Zuerst kommt das Kennenlernen: Der Interessent probiert einen Prototyp für seine Branche selbst aus. Darauf folgt das Vorstellungsgespräch, eine Demo mit einem Klickdummy in seinen eigenen Begriffen. Danach kommt die Probearbeit, ein Pilot mit fünf bis zehn Nutzern und vorab vereinbarten Erfolgskriterien. Erst dann folgt die Festanstellung, also Vertrag und Rollout. Nach drei Monaten gibt es ein Mitarbeitergespräch mit echten Zahlen.

Wir versprechen dabei nichts, was nicht stimmt. In jeder Demo sagen wir klar, was Standard ist, was konfiguriert und was entwickelt werden muss.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du identifizierst passende mittelständische Hersteller mit eigenem Außendienst und findest dort die richtigen Ansprechpartner, vor allem über LinkedIn und den Sales Navigator.
  • Du sprichst Vertriebs- und Serviceleitungen persönlich an, über LinkedIn und am Telefon, und gewinnst sie für ein erstes Gespräch.
  • Du baust dein LinkedIn-Profil zu einer erkennbaren fachlichen Stimme für Außendienstthemen aus.
  • Du qualifizierst eingehende Anfragen von der Website und aus unseren Branchenprototypen.
  • Du führst Demos und stimmst dafür kundenspezifische Prototypen mit unserem Produktteam ab.
  • Du begleitest Interessenten durch ihre Entscheidung und bindest dabei Fachbereich, IT, Geschäftsführung, Datenschutz und Betriebsrat ein.
  • Du verhandelst Pilotprojekte und Verträge.
  • Du bleibst nach dem Vertrag Ansprechpartner für deine Kunden, gemeinsam mit unserem Beratungsteam, und entwickelst die Zusammenarbeit weiter.

Was du mitbringst

  • Du hast mindestens drei Jahre Erfahrung im B2B-Vertrieb, idealerweise mit Software oder erklärungsbedürftigen Lösungen für den Mittelstand.
  • Du hast nachweislich selbst Kunden gewonnen. LinkedIn-Direktansprache und Telefonakquise sind für dich Handwerk.
  • Du schreibst Nachrichten, die nach Mensch klingen, und führst am Telefon ein Gespräch statt eines Skripts.
  • Du hast Erfahrung mit Entscheidungen über mehrere Monate und mehrere Beteiligte, zum Beispiel mit IT-Abteilungen und Betriebsräten.
  • Du sprichst Deutsch auf Muttersprachniveau. Englisch ist ein Plus.
  • Ein großer Vorteil wäre eigene Erfahrung im Außendienst, im Handel oder im technischen Service.

Was du bekommst

  • Gehalt mit Erfolgsbeteiligung: Gute Leistung zahlt sich bei uns aus, auch jenseits der Führungsebene. Wir vergüten nicht nur Abschlüsse, sondern auch qualifizierte Demo-Termine und Erweiterungen bei Bestandskunden.
  • Werkzeuge, die verkaufen helfen: Prototypen, die Interessenten selbst ausprobieren, ein Produktteam, das kundenspezifische Klickdummys in wenigen Tagen baut, LinkedIn Sales Navigator und Zeit für den Aufbau deines Profils.
  • Karriere und Weiterbildung: DMG Academy, Mentoring und Zugriff auf Lernplattformen zu KI, Kundenportalen und mehr.
  • Agiles Arbeiten: Feedback, Mitgestaltung und Verantwortung statt Micromanagement. Du hast kurze Wege zu Geschäftsführung, Produkt und Beratung und echten Einfluss darauf, wie wir in neue Branchen gehen.
  • Arbeitsmodelle nach Maß: Vollzeit, Teilzeit oder remote, mit nur zwei Stunden Kernzeit.
  • Weltweit arbeiten: Du willst von Thailand, Bali oder einem Coworking-Space in Hamburg aus arbeiten? Go for it.
  • Zusatzleistungen: Krankenversicherung, private Rente, Top-Equipment und Zuschüsse.

On behalf of UKRI we are looking for anIdentity & Collaboration Architect(Inside IR35) for an initial 4 month contract. Remote working with occasional office travel.

The Identity & Collaboration Architect will lead the architecture and design of a large-scale Microsoft 365 consolidation programme involving the migration of multiple Microsoft 365 tenancies, mail domains and identity platforms into a single strategic environment.

The role is accountable for developing the future-state architecture for identity, authentication, directory services, email namespace, collaboration services and associated governance models. The architect will work across technical, operational and business stakeholders to establish a coherent, sustainable target operating model that balances organisational requirements with Microsoft's strategic cloud architecture.

A key aspect of the role is the development of target-state identity and namespace strategies, including the transition from multiple independentlymanaged directories and Microsoft 365 tenancies to a consolidated identity platform centred on Microsoft Entra ID.

As an Identity & Collaboration Architect your main responsibilities will be to:

  • Develop target-state identity architecture for a multi-organisational Microsoft 365 environment.
  • Define authoritative sources for identity information and attribute ownership.
  • Establish identity lifecycle architecture covering joiners, movers and leavers.
  • Define future-state email namespace strategy.
  • Develop mail domain architecture covering multiple existing SMTP domains.
  • Analyse impacts of domain consolidation, retention and rationalisation.
  • Support definition of future-state architecture for Microsoft 365 services and ancillary solutions
  • Support tenant consolidation strategy and migration planning.
  • Design core platform services including Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint Online and OneDrive.
  • Develop architectural principles and standards.
  • Establish decision frameworks for identity and namespace management.
  • Lead discovery activities across multiple organisations.
  • Analyse current-state identity, directory and messaging environments.
  • Engage senior stakeholders across IT, security, HR and business functions.
  • Facilitate workshops to define identity, namespace and governance requirements.

Essential:

  • Demonstrable experience in designing and delivering Identity Architecture within complex enterprise environments.
  • Strong understanding of directory services, domain architecture and identity lifecycle management.
  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Entra ID, including authentication, conditional access, identity governance and privileged identity management.
  • Proven experience designing and implementing Microsoft 365 architectures.
  • Experience developing target-state architectures, migration strategies and transition roadmaps across multiple organisations or business units.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to facilitate workshops and present architectural recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Experience defining governance frameworks, operating models and architectural standards.

Desirable:

  • Experience with Microsoft Azure and/or AWS cloud platforms.

1. JOB PURPOSE

To provide strategic and operational leadership of the company's Human Resources function, ensuring the organisation has the people, leadership capability, organisational structure, culture, systems and governance required to deliver its corporate strategy and successfully transition from a credit-only microfinance institution into a fully-fledged, deposit-taking bank regulated by the relevant central bank authorities.

The role will serve as a strategic advisor to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team on workforce strategy, organisational effectiveness, talent, leadership, performance, employee engagement, succession, reward, employee relations and change management.

The Head of Human Resources will be responsible for building a scalable, high-performance and bank-ready people function that supports sustainable business growth while ensuring compliance with employment legislation, regulatory expectations and internal governance standards.

2. STRATEGIC CONTEXT

The company is executing a strategic transformation from a leading credit-only microfinance institution into a fully-fledged, deposit-taking bank regulated by the central bank.

This transformation will require significant organisational, cultural and workforce readiness. The Head of Human Resources will therefore play a critical role in ensuring that the company's people strategy, organisational structure, leadership capability, talent pipeline, policies, performance systems and HR governance evolve in line with the banking transition roadmap.

The role will lead the development of a future-ready workforce capable of operating within a more complex, highly regulated financial-services environment while maintaining the company's entrepreneurial culture and customer-focused orientation.

The priority is to build the right organisation, with the right people, capabilities, leadership and controls, at the right time to support profitable growth and regulatory readiness.

3. KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

A. HR Strategy and Business Partnership

  • Develop and execute the annual Human Resources strategy aligned with the company's corporate strategy and banking transition roadmap.

  • Act as a strategic advisor and trusted business partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team on people, organisational and workforce matters.

  • Translate business strategy into workforce requirements, organisational capability priorities and people initiatives.

  • Provide executive leadership with workforce insights, HR analytics and recommendations to support evidence-based decision-making.

  • Establish HR as a strategic business function with clear service standards, governance and measurable business outcomes.

VP/SVP, Insurance Compliance

Company Description

Lightstone, founded by David Lichtenstein, is one of the most diversified privately held real estate companies in the United States. Headquartered in New York City, Lightstone is active in 27 states across the country, developing, managing, and investing in all sectors of the real estate market, including residential, hospitality, commercial, and retail. With nearly $12 billion in assets under management, Lightstone's portfolio currently includes over 15 million square feet of industrial, logistics, life sciences, and commercial properties, over 25,000 residential units, and over 5,100 hotel keys.

Lightstone's insurance operations comprise a growing multi-entity group of domestic and international insurance companies. The group includes an Arizona-domiciled P&C insurer, an international insurer operating under the Puerto Rico International Insurance Center, a recently acquired 50% interest in a Kansas City-based life and retirement company, and a new life and annuity insurance company currently being formed in either Oklahoma or Arizona.

For more information, please visit www.lightstonegroup.com.

Position Summary

Lightstone is seeking an experienced VP or SVP of Insurance Compliance to manage regulatory compliance across its growing multi-entity insurance and reinsurance group. Reporting to senior leadership, this individual will be responsible for the day-to-day compliance function across a portfolio of domestic P&C, life and annuity, and international insurance companies. The ideal candidate is a hands-on compliance professional with deep regulatory knowledge, strong relationships with state insurance departments, and the ability to keep a complex, multi-jurisdictional insurance operation in good standing with its regulators.

This position reports to the General Counsel and/or Chief Executive Officer.

Key Responsibilities

Multi-Entity Regulatory Compliance

  • Manage ongoing regulatory compliance across all entities in the insurance group
  • Monitor, interpret, and apply insurance laws and regulations across all relevant jurisdictions, including Arizona, Indiana, Oklahoma, and Puerto Rico
  • Ensure all holding company structures, inter-company agreements, affiliated transactions, and enterprise arrangements comply with applicable insurance holding company acts and related statutes
  • Support compliance oversight for the international insurer operating under the Puerto Rico International Insurance Center framework

Examination & Regulatory Relations

  • Lead preparation for and management of all state regulatory examinations, including financial and market conduct examinations
  • Act as a primary point of contact with applicable insurance departments and regulatory bodies
  • Maintain examination readiness programs; ensure all companies are in a continuous state of audit preparedness
  • Respond to regulatory inquiries and work to resolve issues before escalation
  • Prepare, review, and submit all required regulatory filings across all entities and jurisdictions on a timely basis

Transactions, Structures & Agreements

  • Review transactions, inter-company agreements, affiliated arrangements, and reinsurance contracts for regulatory compliance — the group operates primarily as a reinsurance business
  • Support domicile selection, licensing, and regulatory structuring for the new life and annuity company formation
  • Ensure all inter-company transactions and agreements are properly structured, documented, and filed in accordance with applicable law

Financial, Investment & Statutory Compliance

  • Monitor investment management and structuring across entities for compliance with applicable investment laws and statutory requirements
  • Support statutory accounting compliance and the accuracy of regulatory financial reporting
  • Review day-to-day transactions across the group for compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and company policies
  • Escalate financial compliance issues to senior leadership and outside counsel as appropriate

Policies, Training & Compliance Program

  • Develop and maintain compliance policies, procedures, and internal controls across all entities
  • Maintain a compliance calendar tracking all regulatory deadlines, renewal dates, and filing obligations
  • Provide compliance guidance and training to management and staff
  • Coordinate with outside regulatory counsel and compliance consultants as needed

Qualifications

Required

  • Minimum 5-8 years of insurance regulatory compliance experience
  • Working knowledge of NAIC model laws, insurance holding company acts, and multi-state regulatory practices
  • Experience with state insurance department examinations, whether as a regulator, examiner, or company-side compliance professional
  • Ability to manage compliance obligations across multiple entities and jurisdictions simultaneously
  • Strong analytical and writing skills; ability to produce clear regulatory memoranda, compliance summaries, and management-level reports
  • Sound judgment and effective communication skills with regulators, management, and outside counsel

Strongly Preferred

  • Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree from an accredited law school; active bar membership preferred but not required
  • Prior experience working for or with a state insurance department or the NAIC
  • Experience with both P&C and life/annuity compliance
  • Experience supporting insurance company acquisitions or formations
  • Familiarity with reinsurance structures and related regulatory considerations

Personal Attributes

  • Detail-oriented and proactive with a practical, solutions-focused approach
  • Comfortable managing multiple priorities across entities and jurisdictions in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment
  • High integrity and sound judgment; a reliable resource for senior leadership on compliance matters
  • Strong independent work ethic with excellent attention to detail

Compensation & Benefits

Offered salary commensurate with experience, plus discretionary bonus.

$175 - $200k

Architecture & Solution Design

Power Platform & Accelerator Awareness

Soft Skills

Qualifications

jobs.description:
ABOUT CHANGING LIVES PRODUCTIONS:

Changing Lives Productions is the in-house video production company of Dhar Mann Studios, the #1 creator of scripted positive content online. With over 163 million followers and 82+ billion views across YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok, our videos receive more than 1 billion views each month.

We produce several hours of original content weekly with messages of compassion, kindness, and altruism that resonate with viewers of all ages. Our stories tackle real-life challenges and deliver powerful life lessons that resonate with global audiences.

Founded by Dhar Mann, named the “Moral Philosopher of YouTube” by The New York Times, a Time Top 100 Creator, and ranked #2 on Forbes’ 2025 Top Creators list—our founding principle is simple but ambitious: We’re not just telling stories. We’re changing lives.

BIG PICTURE:

We’re looking for an Assistant Editor who keeps our post-production pipeline organized and moving. You’ll collate and prep project files for our VFX and color teams, and manage the digital assets behind every episode we produce.

This is a hands-on support role. You’ll make sure editors, VFX artists, and colorists get clean, complete, correctly structured files on time, and that every piece of footage, project file, and finished master is ingested, organized, backed up, and archived.

Why this role matters

We deliver several hours of original content every week. Missing media, broken links, or poorly prepped turnovers cost our VFX and color teams hours they don’t have.

A well-run library, with clear naming, accurate metadata, and reliable archives, means faster turnarounds, easy re-versioning, and no lost work. You’ll be the person who makes handoffs between editorial, VFX, and color seamless.

HOW YOU’LL SPEND YOUR TIME:

Assistant editorial: file collation and handoffs

  • Collating all project files, media, graphics, music, and SFX for each episode into a complete, correctly structured package
  • Relinking offline media, consolidating projects, and making sure nothing is missing before a handoff
  • Organizing project bins, sequences, and timelines so editors can pick up work without delays
  • Syncing audio and video, and building stringouts or selects when requested
  • Tracking each episode’s status and flagging missing assets or technical issues early

VFX prep

  • Preparing VFX turnovers: exporting plates with handles, reference clips, and EDL/XML files to spec
  • Naming and numbering VFX shots consistently and logging them in the VFX tracker
  • Packaging shot notes, reference frames, and editor instructions with each turnover
  • Bringing returned VFX shots back into the timeline and checking them for sync, frame accuracy, and version

Color prep

  • Preparing locked cuts for color: simplifying timelines, flattening tracks, and removing unsupported effects
  • Exporting XML/AAF/EDL files and reference videos for the colorist
  • Confirming all source media is linked and accessible for the grade
  • Conforming and patching graded media back into the edit, then QC’ing against the reference

Digital asset management

  • Ingesting and verifying camera footage, audio, graphics, and music using checksum-verified offloads
  • Maintaining folder structures, file-naming conventions, and version control across raw footage, projects, and deliverables
  • Logging and tagging assets with accurate, searchable metadata (series, episode, talent, shoot date, usage rights)
  • Uploading all working files and backups to the server in the agreed path, so any editor can pick up a project
  • Creating proxies, transcodes, and alternate versions (textless, clean, localized) as needed
  • Exporting and QC’ing final masters to spec (resolution, codec, aspect ratio, captions, loudness)
  • Archiving completed projects to long-term cloud and offline storage, and retrieving archived media on request
  • Monitoring storage capacity and keeping drives and servers clean per retention guidelines
  • Keeping asset trackers, delivery logs, and archive records up to date

WHAT YOU HAVE:

  • 3–5+ years of experience as an assistant editor, media manager, or in post-production operations
  • Strong proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro, including Project Manager, consolidating and relinking media, and proxy workflows
  • Hands-on experience preparing VFX turnovers and color handoffs (EDL, XML, AAF, plates with handles)
  • Working knowledge of codecs, formats, frame rates, resolutions, and export settings, and the ability to spot technical issues during QC
  • Exceptional organization and attention to detail, with the discipline to keep naming, folder structures, and metadata consistent under tight deadlines
  • An understanding of backup and archival best practices (3-2-1 rule, checksum verification with tools like Hedge or ShotPut Pro, cloud and LTO storage)
  • Proficiency with Google Sheets, Excel, or Airtable for tracking assets, turnovers, and deliveries
  • Clear, proactive communication, especially when flagging missing files or delays

Nice to have

  • Familiarity with DaVinci Resolve and After Effects
  • Experience with DAM/MAM and review platforms (Frame.io, Iconik, Air, CatDV, or similar) and shared storage (Google Drive, Dropbox, LucidLink)
  • Basic understanding of music licensing, clearances, and usage rights
  • Experience in a high-volume content studio or episodic workflow

WHO OVERSEES YOU:

The Assistant Editor reports to the Jr. Post Production Manager.

WHO YOU OVERSEE:

No direct reports at this time.

WHERE IT ALL GOES DOWN:

You’ll work remotely from home or a personal office and log hours in Dhar Mann Studios’ time-tracking software.

WHEN THE MAGIC HAPPENS:

The typical schedule is 40 hours per week. Specific hours and shift overlap with the US team will be discussed during interviews

Salary: $15

jobs.description:
AI Technology Partners (AITP) is a leader in delivering cutting-edge generative AI solutions and managed services, specializing in secure, customizable AI deployments for enterprises. Our offerings are designed to help organizations unlock the full value of AI while maintaining robust security and compliance across their infrastructures.

About the role

At AI Technology Partners (AITP), we empower enterprises to scale revenue & profit —with secure, compliant generative AI solutions.

In this role, you’ll lead the design and delivery of agentic systems that orchestrate tools, data, and policies to solve real business workflows—safely, reliably, and at scale. If you like greenfield architecture, fast iteration, and measurable impact with enterprise clients, this is your playground.

What you'll do

Architecture & System Design (Agentic)

  • Design multi-agent architectures with robust state management, memory, and routing.
  • Choose and implement leading frameworks such as LangGraph/LangChain Agents, Microsoft AutoGen, CrewAI, LlamaIndex Agents, Semantic Kernel, or Haystack Agents—and justify trade-offs.
  • Build modular components (planners, tool registries, policy guards, evaluators) that are reusable across clients and domains.

Tooling & Orchestration

  • Integrate enterprise tools and data sources via function/tool calling, webhooks, and event-driven flows (Queues/Service Bus/Functions).
  • Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns with vector stores (Azure AI Search, pgvector, MongoDB Atlas, Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus) and structured knowledge (SQL/Graph).
  • Add deterministic fallbacks, circuit breakers, and caching to keep latency and cost predictable.

Reliability, Observability & MLOps

  • Define SLIs/SLOs for agent runs; implement tracing, metrics, and logging (e.g., Langfuse + OpenTelemetry) and build dashboards for run-level analytics.
  • Create evaluation harnesses (automatic + human-in-the-loop) using tools such as Ragas, DeepEval, promptfoo to measure groundedness, task success, safety, and cost.
  • Productionize with CI/CD, environment promotion, feature flags, and canary strategies; optimize cost-per-task and time-to-success.

Safety, Security & Governance

  • Enforce content and safety policies (redaction, classification, guardrails) with policy-as-code; implement role/tenant isolation and data minimization.
  • Collaborate with security teams to align to ISO 27001/SOC 2/NIST/HIPAA/GDPR contexts; deliver audit-ready evidence for agentic workflows.
  • Build privacy-first patterns (no data exfiltration by default, least-privilege tool access, secure prompt/trace storage).

Product & Client Impact

  • Work directly with enterprise client teams to translate business processes into agentic designs; present trade-offs and proofs-of-value that lead to production.
  • Partner with solution leads to create domain-specific agents (e.g., RFP assist, incident RCA drafting, knowledge ops) and reusable templates.

Qualifications

Must-have

  • 5–8+ years in software/platform engineering with recent production LLM applications (not just prototypes).
  • Hands-on expertise with agentic frameworks (one or more of: LangGraph/LangChain Agents, AutoGen, CrewAI, LlamaIndex Agents, Semantic Kernel, Haystack Agents) and tool/function-calling patterns.
  • Strong RAG engineering across vector DBs, chunking/embedding strategies, metadata/search ranking, and grounding techniques.
  • Proven track record building observable, cost-aware, and secure LLM systems (tracing, evals, guardrails, secrets/IAM, PII handling).
  • Solid software engineering fundamentals: Python/TypeScript, async patterns, APIs, testing, CI/CD, containerization.
  • Clear communicator who can interface with clients and write crisp technical docs.

Nice to have

  • Azure-first experience (Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Studio, Azure Functions/Container Apps/AKS, Private Link/VNet, Key Vault, Entra ID).
  • Cross-cloud exposure (AWS/GCP) and hybrid integrations; experience with enterprise connectors (SharePoint/OneDrive, ServiceNow, Salesforce).
  • Experience with structured output, constrained decoding, JSON Schemas, and program-of-thought planning.

Location

  • Remote, US-based candidates preferred. The role may involve working across multiple time zones.

How we work

  • Ownership & velocity: Small team, big surface area. You’ll design, ship, and iterate quickly.
  • Security by design: Data governance and safety are table stakes, not afterthoughts.
  • Evidence over vibes: We measure task success, grounding, and cost—and improve with data.
  • AI as leverage: We use LLMs to accelerate engineering—not replace it.

Compensation

  • We offer a competitive and flexible compensation package aligned to experience, scope, and engagement model. This may include base salary, performance incentives, and equity participation, designed to reward meaningful contributions and impact.

What we offer

  • Challenging work on meaningful, production agentic systems for enterprise clients.
  • Learning & sharing culture with deep dives, brown bags, and support for certifications/publication.
  • Inclusive, flexible workplace—bring your whole self; work where you do your best thinking.

How to Apply
Interested candidates are encouraged to submit their resumes and a brief cover letter outlining relevant experience and why they are a good fit for this role.

ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest.

ProPublica’s Local Reporting Network helps produce vital, investigative journalism in communities where such stories would otherwise not be done. Now entering its ninth year, the program will be taking on 15 new partnerships over the course of 2026.

Applications for all 15 projects are open now and will be considered on a rolling basis using the deadlines below. There will be three fellowship periods and we will select five fellows for each round:

  • Spring cohort - This round is now closed.
    • Application deadline: Rolling, no later than Feb. 5, 2026, by 11:59 p.m. ET.
    • Open to: All applicants from English-language local and regional newsrooms in the United States and its territories.
    • Fellowship dates: April 1, 2026, through March 31, 2027.
  • Summer cohort. This round is now closed
    • Application deadline: Rolling, no later than May 1, 2026.
    • Open to: Newsrooms in the states listed as eligible through our 50 State Initiative.
    • Fellowships dates: July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027.
  • Fall cohort
    • Application deadline: Rolling, no later thanJuly 27, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET.
    • Open to: Newsrooms in the remaining states listed as eligible through our 50 State Initiative. (Note: This list of states will be updated in July 2025.)
    • Fellowship dates: Oct. 1, 2026, through Sept. 30, 2027.

For these partnerships, ProPublica will provide a grant, to be paid in monthly installments, to the selected newsroom reflecting the annual salary (up to $80,000 plus a 25% allowance for benefits) for one full-time reporter in each newsroom. Successful candidates will have a proven track record of investigative reporting and impact, and will provide a memo about the project they’re proposing working on for the duration of the one-year partnership.

Strong applications will express why the project needs to be told in your community — we’re eager for projects that can’t be done anywhere else. They will also explain how the project would benefit from this collaboration, potentially including the role that our data, research and engagement reporting resources could play, and they will discuss how the project may resonate with both local and national audiences.

Once accepted, local reporters will work from and report to their home newsrooms while receiving extensive support and guidance for their work from ProPublica, including collaboration with a senior editor and access to the nonprofit newsroom’s expertise. The work will be published or broadcast by your newsroom and simultaneously by ProPublica.

ProPublica reporters and editors are available to answer questions or to give you feedback on your application before you submit it. Please reach us at .

We are unable to accept applications via email. No phone calls, please.

  • Framework Standardizing: Implement modern product operating model principles (e.g., product trios, data-informed decision making, rapid prototyping, and de-risking assumptions).
  • Evangelize Kaizen: Introduce continuous feedback loops and structured retrospective frameworks to scale product management maturity across the entire organization.

2. Product Ownership: Advanced Ads

  • Strategy & Vision: Define and execute the long-term product vision for Advanced Ads, integrating its flexible ad injection, targeting, and Google Ad Manager capabilities deeper into the MonetizeMore ecosystem.
  • Continuous Discovery: Lead continuous product discovery to uncover publishers' deepest pain points, validating ideas for usability, feasibility, viability, and value before writing code.
  • Revenue & Growth: Take end-to-end ownership from monetization strategy to GTM. Prioritize the roadmap based on clear ROI, keeping a laser focus on customer lifetime value (LTV) and monthly recurring revenue (MRR).

jobs.description:
the role

This is a remote-first (UK-based) role, with access to our London office and/or other WeWork coworking spaces across the country. Some in-person attendance is expected for board and leadership meetings, plus international travel as required.

We are looking for a commercially intuitive General Counsel to lead the legal function of our established and rapidly scaling AI business as we launch our flagship innovation, Workspace, to market. This is a senior leadership role covering UK legal matters, with oversight across major international jurisdictions. You will support a growing global customer base in sectors including media and entertainment, retail, healthcare and the public sector.

You will be a trusted member of the executive leadership team, supported directly by the c suite and balancing legal risk management with pragmatic, business-focused advice.
You will build on the foundations of our existing legal function, with real freedom to shape how the department works moving forwards. The legal team’s structure, ways of working and tools are yours to design as you grow a high-performing in-house team. You will oversee external counsel relationships and own Stelia's legal, compliance, governance and regulatory frameworks as we expand globally.

Uniquely, you will build the legal function's technology on Stelia's own platform. You will act as an internal design partner to our product and engineering teams, and make legal a showcase for what our technology can do.

what you'll do

1. Corporate & Governance

  • Advise the Board and CEO on corporate structure, governance and shareholder matters.
  • Lead legal due diligence for upcoming funding rounds.
  • Oversee company secretarial duties, board meetings and statutory filings in the UK and internationally.
  • Draft, review and negotiate shareholder agreements and investment documentation.

2. Product Launch & Go-to-Market

  • Ensure the legal and regulatory foundations for the continuous development of Stelia's technologies are in place, and scale them as adoption grows.
  • Own Stelia's customer-facing terms, including master services and SaaS agreements, acceptable use policies, SLAs and data processing agreements.
  • Maintain Stelia's positions on AI-specific contract issues, including ownership of outputs, IP indemnities for generated content, use of customer data for model training and performance disclaimers.
  • Review marketing materials and product claims so that statements about AI capabilities are accurate and defensible.
  • Advise on sector-specific requirements in target markets with external support, such as medical device and clinical safety rules in healthcare, and procurement, security accreditation and transparency obligations in the public sector.

3. Commercial Contracts

  • Introduce tools and processes that streamline contracting, balancing efficiency with Stelia's risk appetite and growth trajectory.
  • Establish playbooks for scalable contract management across a global client base.
  • Lead the negotiation and drafting of complex technology, SaaS, licensing, distribution and strategic partnership agreements.

4. Data Protection, AI Regulation & Compliance

  • Act as the company's lead on data privacy, leading compliance with the UK GDPR, EU GDPR, CCPA and other international frameworks.
  • Classify Stelia's products under the EU AI Act and other emerging AI regimes, and run the resulting transparency, documentation and governance obligations.
  • Monitor and advise on developing AI legislation and ethical frameworks globally, and lead the strategy for managing conflicting requirements between jurisdictions.
  • Oversee export controls and sanctions compliance as Stelia sells internationally.
  • Partner with product and engineering teams to embed legal and regulatory compliance in product development.
  • Develop internal compliance policies and training programmes.

5. Legal Technology & Operations

  • Build the legal function's technology stack on Stelia's own platform and in-house models.
  • Act as an internal design partner to product and engineering, translating legal workflows into clear product requirements and feeding back on early tools.
  • Position the legal function as a reference use case for Stelia's technology, supporting customer conversations where useful.
  • Set governance for using AI tools on confidential and privileged material, covering legal privilege, access controls and data retention.

6. Employment & People

  • Line-manage Stelia's VP of People (or equivalent).
  • Oversee employment law compliance in the UK and coordinate with international counsel and employers of record for global hiring.
  • Own the legal framework for remote-first working, including staff working from abroad (tax, permanent establishment and immigration risk), remote working policies and health and safety for home workers.
  • Keep employment contracts compliant and maintain consultancy agreements.
  • Manage the administration of employee and advisor incentive schemes, including liaising with accountants on valuations.
  • Advise on employee disputes, restructurings and cross-border HR matters.

7. Intellectual Property

  • Lead IP strategy to protect proprietary AI models, code, datasets and related technology.
  • Manage Stelia's trademark and patent portfolios, working with the COO and CAIO to identify new registration needs through the product development lifecycle.
  • Advise on open-source software use and licensing risks.

8. Disputes & Risk Management

  • Proactively identify, assess and mitigate legal and regulatory risks.
  • Manage litigation, arbitration and IP disputes globally, working with external counsel where needed.
  • Advise on client and vendor disputes, settlement negotiations and contract enforcement.
  • Provide legal input into crisis management, incident response and data breach notification processes.

9. Leadership & Strategy

  • Build and manage a high-performing in-house legal team as we scale.
  • Act as a key strategic advisor to the CEO and executive team on growth, customer sectors and international expansion.
  • Build strong relationships with regulators, industry bodies and external stakeholders.
  • Represent Stelia publicly on the regulatory pressures facing the AI industry.

Your First 12 Months

  • Continue to develop the legal and regulatory foundations for Workspace, and scale them as customer adoption grows.
  • Build out the company's global legal framework, policies and compliance programme.
  • Stand up the legal function's technology stack on Stelia's own platform, and implement scalable processes for contract negotiation and management.
  • Provide executive-level legal input on fundraising, partnerships and international expansion.
  • Oversee international subsidiary incorporation as customer or employee growth requires.
  • Position Stelia as a leader in ethical and legally compliant AI deployment.

who we're looking for

Experience & Qualifications

  • Qualified lawyer in England & Wales with at least 7 years' PQE.
  • Experience in a high-growth technology company (AI or deep tech preferred).
  • Background in commercial contracts, IP and data protection preferred but other specialisms considered.
  • Experience taking a technology product to market, including customer terms and regulatory readiness (preferred).
  • Familiarity with international regulatory frameworks governing technology, data and AI, and insight into the ethical considerations surrounding AI.
  • Experience managing legal issues across multiple jurisdictions (preferred).
  • Previous exposure to fundraising and M&A (preferred).

Skills & Competencies

  • Ability to balance risk with business objectives, and to prioritise the work that enables growth.
  • Excellent negotiation and stakeholder management skills.
  • Strong leadership, with experience building and managing legal teams.
  • Ability to translate complex legal issues into clear, actionable advice for non-lawyers.
  • Comfortable working directly with engineers, testing early-stage tools and articulating legal workflows as product requirements.
  • High ethical standards, with a proactive approach to governance and compliance.

Personal Attributes

  • Strategic thinker with a growth mindset.
  • Collaborative, resilient and adaptable, and comfortable with fast-shifting priorities in a dynamic market.
  • Comfortable creating structure where it does not yet exist.
  • Effective in a remote-first team, communicating clearly in writing and across time zones.
  • Willing and enthusiastic to provide industry commentary, with a legal slant, as part of Stelia's leadership team.
  • Global outlook, with cultural awareness and sensitivity to diverse jurisdictions.
  • Passion for AI and emerging technologies, with curiosity about their legal and ethical implications and about legal technology's potential to improve compliance and company management.
  • Understands the importance of strategic partnerships within the tech ecosystem, and is willing to build relationships beyond the legal sector.

what you can expect from us

  • Meaningful work on problems that are still being defined
  • Early ownership and the opportunity to shape your work
  • A culture where ideas are openly challenged and explored
  • Working alongside highly capable, ambitious peers
  • A remote-first, flexible environment built on trust
And let’s not forget some of our benefits… With us, you can enjoy:
  • £120,000 - £140,000 depending on experience
  • Unlimited holiday
  • £200 equipment budget to get you set up to work best, whether that’s at home or in our office
  • Enhanced sick pay and family leave offerings
  • Company-wide bonus scheme
  • Share options
  • Access to our London office and other WeWork locations

jobs.title: Manager, Marketing Data & Analytics
jobs.excerpt: How will you make a difference to PMI?  The Manager, Marketing Data and Analytics owns the business data architecture and metric definitions behind Marketing's numbers, and leads the team that measures Marketing.
jobs.description:
How will you make a difference to PMI? The Manager, Marketing Data and Analytics owns the business data architecture and metric definitions behind Marketing's numbers, and leads the team that measures Marketing. The role defines how marketing, customer, product, and revenue data should be modeled, decides what each metric means, and ensures those definitions are implemented consistently across Snowflake, BI, and natural-language analytics. The role combines hands-on technical depth with team leadership. The individual is expected to be advanced in SQL, to design analytical data models, and to profile, reconcile, and diagnose data directly, so they can specify what engineering builds and verify that the result represents the business correctly. They are equally expected to lead three to four analysts, set the standards those analysts work to, and develop the team's technical capability. Data Engineering and the Snowflake team own ingestion, infrastructure, orchestration, transformation pipelines, and semantic view implementation. This role represents Marketing in the design of the data layer, writes the specifications those teams build against, and is accountable for ensuring the resulting data products correctly represent the business.

What you’ll bring to the role:

Business Data Architecture, Metric Definitions, and Context

Own Marketing's canonical metric definitions and the business logic the governed semantic layer implements, and arbitrate those definitions when marketing, finance, and reporting platforms disagree. Specify the semantic models for the most complex and cross-domain marketing use cases, and validate what the Snowflake team builds against that specification. Own the business data architecture for Marketing, defining the facts, dimensions, grain, relationships, hierarchies, and conformed dimensions that connect marketing, customer, product, transaction, and engagement data. Design analytical models that answer cross-domain questions spanning acquisition, engagement, conversion, certification, membership, renewal, and revenue. Write advanced SQL to profile data, validate sources, reconcile metrics, build reusable datasets, and investigate complex customer and business questions. Determine what unstructured content, such as business documentation, definitions, and prior analyses, must be retrievable alongside structured metrics for natural-language and agent-based analysis, and maintain source-to-metric mappings and lineage. Own the business questions, expected results, and synonym glossary behind the Verified Query Repository supporting Cortex Analyst and natural-language analytics. Own the context layer that makes Marketing's data interpretable to analysts and AI agents, including entity descriptions, metric documentation, approved analytical uses, and known limitations of each source. Diagnose discrepancies across Snowflake, BI, Adobe Analytics, marketing platforms, finance reporting, and operational systems. Identify gaps in source data, identity resolution, event structures, and dimensional consistency before they become downstream reporting issues. Define ownership boundaries between source systems, engineered data products, semantic models, and reporting layers.

Team Leadership and Capability

Lead, coach, and develop a team of three to four analysts spanning paid media, customer and lifecycle analytics, and digital analytics. Set the Marketing Analytics roadmap, allocate the team against it, and manage intake and prioritization from across Marketing. Establish and enforce analytical standards including SQL quality, peer review, testing, documentation, and reuse. Review the team's models, queries, and analyses before they reach stakeholders, and hold the quality bar for what gets published. Grow the team's depth in dimensional modeling, data modeling practice, and analytical rigor through direct coaching and review. Manage performance, hiring, and development planning for the team.

Marketing Measurement and Performance Analytics

Define and govern core marketing KPIs including revenue, conversion, CAC and CPA, ROAS, retention, funnel progression, pacing to plan, and channel efficiency. Own the integrity and narrative of recurring executive performance reporting, including monthly business reviews and QBR analytics, with the team producing the underlying analysis. Determine how platform-reported, attribution-based, financial, and incrementality-based measures reconcile, and establish where each is appropriately used. Lead attribution, cohort, and incrementality work so it produces decision-grade guidance on marketing investment, building the harder analyses directly. Own predictive modeling for Marketing, including membership churn and renewal propensity, certification lapse and recertification likelihood, and product and cross-sell propensity, alongside segmentation, lifecycle, and cohort analysis across CRM, web, campaign, commerce, certification, and membership data. Define the features, target definitions, validation approach, and performance thresholds for predictive models, determine when a score is reliable enough to act on, and establish how scores are refreshed, monitored for drift, and activated in campaign, lifecycle, and retention programs. Set analytical standards for A/B testing, holdouts, geo experiments, and conversion-lift studies within the marketing analytics practice, including hypotheses, test populations, success metrics, and readouts. Partner with Product and Marketing to define measurable funnels, customer states, lifecycle stages, and behavioral signals for considered-purchase journeys, and hold a clear distinction between attribution, correlation, prediction, and causal measurement when results are communicated.

Analytics Delivery and Enablement

Govern Marketing's analytical products in enterprise BI and visualization platforms, ensuring definitions are sourced from the semantic layer rather than rebuilt in the tool. Use Adobe Analytics to investigate digital behavior, traffic, customer journeys, and conversion performance, and work with data from Adobe Experience Platform, CRM, commerce, and paid media systems. Apply working knowledge of digital event instrumentation, tagging, identity, and schemas to identify measurement and architecture issues at the source, and establish where AI-assisted tooling is applied to SQL development, analysis, documentation, and testing. Expand governed self-service and AI-assisted analytics for Marketing across Snowflake, BI, and natural-language surfaces, and represent Marketing data and context requirements in the Marketing AI reference architecture. Define what Marketing data and context AI agents and natural-language tools are permitted to reach, at what grain, and under what access and accuracy controls, and own the evaluation approach that tests answer accuracy before release and monitors it as data and definitions change.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Serve as Marketing's primary analytical counterpart to Data Engineering, Data Architecture, and Data Governance. Translate business questions into analytical requirements and data-product specifications that engineering can build against. Partner with Data Engineering on transformation logic, data contracts, source integration, model design, and data-quality requirements. Partner with Performance Marketing, Brand, Digital, Product, Lifecycle, and Regional Marketing on measurement needs and analytical priorities. Present analytical findings, performance trends, and recommendations to senior leadership.

Scope of Role Leads a team of three to four analysts covering marketing, customer, and performance analytics, while personally designing analytical data models and validating them. Accountable for Marketing's business data architecture, metric definitions, context layer, predictive models, and executive performance reporting across certification, membership, e-learning, events, and other product lines. Hands-on ownership concentrates in data model design, metric reconciliation, predictive model validation, evaluation of analytical accuracy, and diagnosis of cross-system discrepancies. Semantic view implementation sits with the Snowflake team, built to this role's specification. Routine reporting, campaign analysis, and dashboard production sit with the team, under this role's review and standards. Data Engineering, Technology, and the Snowflake team own ingestion, infrastructure, orchestration, platform access, transformation pipelines, and semantic view implementation. Enterprise data governance policy, cataloging, and cross-domain stewardship sit outside this role; the incumbent partners with Data Governance and applies those standards within Marketing.

Role Qualifications:
