Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Reliability Automation

Position Overview

Autodesk is the global leader in design and make technology, including industry-leading 3D design, engineering, and entertainment software and services, that offer customers better outcomes through automation and insights for their design and make processes. If you’ve ever driven a high-performance car, admired a towering skyscraper, used a smartphone, or watched a great film, chances are you’ve experienced what millions of Autodesk customers are doing with our software.


Want to help make a better world? As a Senior Site Reliability Engineer at Autodesk, you can help us build and operate reliable, secure, and scalable cloud services for Autodesk products and customers.

As part of an SRE team focused on Reliability Automation, you will have a unique opportunity to help shape how Autodesk detects, responds to, and engineers away production issues at scale. This is a project-oriented, engineering-heavy role where you will build the automation, tooling, and platform capabilities that other engineering teams rely on to run their services reliably.

You will combine software engineering and production operations to automate how Autodesk services are operated, monitored, recovered, and validated. You will partner closely with product engineering, platform, infrastructure, and operations teams to turn manual operational work into durable, reusable automation.

The ideal candidate is a strong software engineer who is drawn to operational problems. You should be comfortable designing and shipping production-grade software, and equally comfortable reasoning about how distributed systems fail. Success in this role requires strong technical judgment, the ability to drive projects end to end, and a passion for replacing manual operational work with durable engineering.

Responsibilities

  • Lead reliability automation projects end to end, from problem definition and design through delivery, adoption, and measurable impact on availability, performance, and operational efficiency.
  • Design, develop, and maintain shared automation, tooling, and platform services that improve the reliability, scalability, and operability of production systems across Autodesk.
  • Partner with engineering teams to understand their operational pain, and drive adoption of the automation and reliability capabilities your team builds.
  • Instrument and automate reliability signals such as SLOs/SLIs, error budgets, and alerting-as-code, so teams get reliability measurement by default rather than by manual effort.
  • Build automation that improves deployment safety, operational efficiency, and service recovery, including self-healing and auto-remediation capabilities.
  • Automate incident response workflows, diagnostics, and runbook execution to reduce time to detect, time to mitigate, and manual intervention.
  • Extend monitoring, alerting, logging, and tracing capabilities, and automate their coverage and consistency across services.
  • Own the reliability, availability, and operability of the automation and platform services your team runs, including on-call response when they fail.
  • Turn incident and post-incident findings from across the organization into automation, tooling, and durable engineering fixes.
  • Design and scale automated resilience testing, chaos engineering, Gameday, and disaster recovery tooling to validate system behavior and recovery capabilities.
  • Continuously identify and eliminate operational toil through software engineering, automation, and process improvement.
  • Ensure the automation and services your team builds meet Autodesk security, privacy, and operational risk requirements.
  • Participate in a 24x7 on-call rotation for the automation, tooling, and platform services owned by the team.
  • Function effectively in a fast-paced environment while helping mature reliability automation practices across engineering.

Basic Qualifications

  • B.S. or higher in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 7+ years of experience in Software Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering, Platform Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals, including API and service design, testing, code review, and shipping production-grade software.
  • Working knowledge of reliability engineering concepts such as SLOs/SLIs, observability, incident response, and toil reduction, and experience applying them in practice.
  • Experience building on AWS, Azure, or another public cloud platform.
  • Strong programming skills in languages such as Python, Go, Java, or similar.
  • Experience with Infrastructure as Code, CI/CD pipelines, and deployment automation.
  • Ability to work independently, scope ambiguous problems, and drive projects to completion across team boundaries.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience building software and automation for production systems.
  • Experience building self-healing, auto-remediation, or event-driven operational automation.
  • Experience building internal platforms, developer tooling, or services adopted by other engineering teams.
  • Experience building or adopting AI-assisted operational tooling, such as LLM-based incident triage, diagnostics, or agentic remediation workflows.
  • Experience with containers, Kubernetes, cloud-native architectures, APIs, and distributed systems.
  • Experience integrating with observability platforms such as Splunk, Dynatrace, Datadog, CloudWatch, or similar.
  • Experience with event-driven architectures, workflow orchestration, or job scheduling systems.
  • Experience with incident management platforms such as incident.io, FireHydrant, or PagerDuty, and automating workflows on top of them.
  • Experience designing and implementing operational automation at scale.
  • Experience building or automating Gamedays, chaos experiments, disaster recovery exercises, or resilience testing.

Join Tether and Shape the Future of Digital Finance

At Tether, we’re not just building products, we’re pioneering a global financial revolution. Our cutting-edge solutions empower businesses—from exchanges and wallets to payment processors and ATMs—to seamlessly integrate reserve-backed tokens across blockchains. By harnessing the power of blockchain technology, Tether enables you to store, send, and receive digital tokens instantly, securely, and globally, all at a fraction of the cost. Transparency is the bedrock of everything we do, ensuring trust in every transaction.

Innovate with Tether

Tether Finance: Our innovative product suite features the world’s most trusted stablecoin, USDT, relied upon by hundreds of millions worldwide, alongside pioneering digital asset tokenization services.

But that’s just the beginning:

Tether Power: Driving sustainable growth, our energy solutions optimize excess power for Bitcoin mining using eco-friendly practices in state-of-the-art, geo-diverse facilities.

Tether Data: Fueling breakthroughs in AI and peer-to-peer technology, we reduce infrastructure costs and enhance global communications with cutting-edge solutions like KEET, our flagship app that redefines secure and private data sharing.

Tether Education: Democratizing access to top-tier digital learning, we empower individuals to thrive in the digital and gig economies, driving global growth and opportunity.

Tether Evolution: At the intersection of technology and human potential, we are pushing the boundaries of what is possible, crafting a future where innovation and human capabilities merge in powerful, unprecedented ways.

Why Join Us?

Our team is a global talent powerhouse, working remotely from every corner of the world. If you’re passionate about making a mark in the fintech space, this is your opportunity to collaborate with some of the brightest minds, pushing boundaries and setting new standards. We’ve grown fast, stayed lean, and secured our place as a leader in the industry.

If you have excellent English communication skills and are ready to contribute to the most innovative platform on the planet, Tether is the place for you.

Are you ready to be part of the future?

About the job

QV.AC is a general purpose AI assistant that runs locally on your devices, it gives users greater control over their data and how they use artificial intelligence. Our focus is on local, on-device, and privacy-preserving AI, with opportunities to connect these experiences across Tether’s peer-to-peer ecosystem.

We’re looking for a Product Manager with a strong interest in AI and a practical understanding of how to turn emerging capabilities into useful products.

You will work closely with the Product Lead to help advance the QV.AC vision: identifying valuable use cases, defining AI features, exploring product concepts, and working with engineering and design to bring them to users. You’ll contribute to product direction and take responsibility for moving assigned features from discovery through delivery and iteration.

This role suits someone who knows how to leverage AI to the maximum and enjoys experimenting with new AI technologies, understands its possibilities and limitations, and cares about making complex technology easy to use.

Responsibilities

  • Help shape AI features: Work with the Product Lead to translate thevision into concrete use cases, feature proposals, and product requirements. Bring ideas grounded in user needs, research, and hands-on experimentation.

  • Understand users and their problems: Gather feedback, conduct research, and explore how people use AI in their everyday workflows. Identify where AI can solve a meaningful problem and where a simpler solution may work better.

  • Turn ideas into clear specifications: Write product briefs, user stories, acceptance criteria, and user flows that help engineering and design understand the intended experience, constraints, and measures of success.

  • Prototype and explore: Create wireframes, mockups, and working prototypes to test ideas and communicate product behavior. Use AI-assisted tools to explore concepts quickly and refine them with the team.

  • Collaborate on technical trade-offs: Work with engineers to understand what is feasible across devices and models. Help assess the impact of response quality, latency, memory usage, battery consumption, and privacy on the user experience.

  • Support prioritization and planning: Help the Product Lead evaluate opportunities, clarify scope, identify dependencies, and maintain a focused backlog aligned with product priorities.

  • Drive feature delivery: Follow assigned features through development, resolve product questions, review the experience, and coordinate feedback and release readiness with relevant teams.

  • Stay close to AI developments: Explore new AI products, models, tools, and interaction patterns, and explain their practical relevance to. Share clear recommendations about what is worth testing or adopting and why.

Requirements

Mandatory:

  • 7+ years of product management experience, ideally working on AI software products with technical engineering teams.

  • Practical experience building, shipping, or prototyping AI-powered features, with the ability to explain your contribution and what you learned.

  • A working understanding of AI concepts such as inference, harnesses, model capabilities and limitations, context, and evaluation, alongside an interest in local and on-device AI.

  • The ability to translate an ambiguous idea into a clear user problem, proposed solution, and actionable requirements.

  • Strong product judgment, with attention to usability, scope, and measurable user value.

  • Confidence creating prototypes using design or coding tools

  • Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to discuss technical trade-offs with engineers and explain them to non-technical colleagues.

  • A proactive, collaborative approach: comfortable taking responsibility for your work, asking questions early, and incorporating feedback.

  • Familiarity with product analytics, user research, and iterative software development.

Preferred:

  • Experience with local AI, on-device inference, or open-source models.

  • Experience building AI assistants, conversational interfaces, or multimodal features.

  • Familiarity with desktop or mobile product development.

  • An understanding of peer-to-peer technologies and decentralized applications.

  • Experience evaluating AI output quality and designing user experiences that account for uncertainty and errors.

  • Experience working in a distributed team.

Important information for candidates
Recruitment scams have become increasingly common. To protect yourself, please keep the following in mind when applying for roles:

  • Apply only through our official channels. We do not use third-party platforms or agencies for recruitment unless clearly stated. All open roles are listed on our official careers page:

  • Verify the recruiter’s identity. All our recruiters have verified LinkedIn profiles. If you’re unsure, you can confirm their identity by checking their profile or contacting us through our website.

  • Be cautious of unusual communication methods. We do not conduct interviews over WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS. All communication is done through official company emails and platforms.

  • Double-check email addresses. All communication from us will come from emails ending in @ or @

  • We will never request payment or financial details. If someone asks for personal financial information or payment at any point during the hiring process, it is a scam. Please report it immediately.

When in doubt, feel free to reach out through our official website.

jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

A fast-growing, highly entrepreneurial group operating across property investment, portfolio assets, and professional training is looking for a commercially minded, analytical FP&A Manager to join their expanding global finance function. Operating fully remotely from South Africa on a full-time, permanent basis, this position balances high operational accountability with a deeply supportive, progressive team culture.
The core working hours align directly with UK business hours, running Monday to Friday from 08:30 to 16:30 UK time (with an early start preferred for a self-starter who likes to hit the ground running). In South African local time, depending on daylight saving and seasonal clock shifts, this translates to an attractive daytime shift pattern of 09:30 AM – 17:30 PM / 10:30 AM – 18:30 PM SAST.
Known for fostering exceptional cross-border team integration, the group is modernising its management reporting and strategic finance operations. In this role, you will take end-to-end ownership of group budgeting, rolling cash forecasts, and monthly management accounts across multiple active entities.
Key Responsibilities
  • Management Accounts Ownership: Lead the complete month-end close across multiple operating entities, producing comprehensive Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow statements.
  • Close Acceleration: Drive process improvements to streamline the reporting timetable, accelerating the monthly close down to working day 5.
  • Commercial Storytelling & Variance Analysis: Unpick large volumes of complex data and deliver clear, plain-language variance commentary to operational heads and senior leadership.
  • Rolling Forecasts & Budgets: Build, maintain, and refine rolling cash flow models and group budgets, tracking actual performance against business plans and highlighting risks early.
  • Accounting Controls & Accruals: Oversee balance sheet reconciliations, embed accrual accounting discipline across business units, and support statutory compliance schedules.
  • Systems, Automation & AI: Continuously enhance financial models and reporting packs through advanced spreadsheet automation, multiple financial systems, and modern AI tools.
  • Team Mentorship & Operational Support: Provide hands-on guidance, training, and development to two UK-based Accounts Assistants and an incoming Credit Controller, providing operational cover when required.

Requirements

  • Professional Accreditation (Essential): Fully qualified accountant (CIMA, ACCA, CA(SA) / ACA).
  • Experience: Minimum 3–5+ years in FP&A, management accounting, or senior financial analysis, with demonstrated ownership of multi-entity reporting and variance analysis.
  • Software & Systems: Advanced Excel skills (ability to unpick large datasets and build complex models) and hands-on proficiency in Xero are essential. Experience with Syft Analytics or BI reporting tools is a strong advantage.
  • Curiosity & Communication: Exceptional communication and presentation skills—confident in presenting financial insights to non-financial stakeholders and partnering with division heads.
  • Work Style: High autonomy and ownership; a self-starter who thrives working independently across multiple systems.
  • Industry Background (Advantageous): Prior experience in property, lettings, or asset management is a plus, but applications from other fast-paced commercial industries are warmly welcomed.
  • Workspace Setup: A dedicated home office environment equipped with high-speed fibre internet and reliable backup power solutions (UPS / inverter) to guarantee uninterrupted operational availability.

Benefits

  • Long-term stability within an international, full-time permanent remote role.
  • A collaborative, supportive leadership team with structured onboarding, peer support, and ongoing professional development.
  • A visible seat at the table where your commercial insights directly shape executive decisions and group growth.

jobs.description:
PAVE Insight is a market intelligence firm focused on fleet telematics within the connected mobility industry. We provide data and insights on telematics providers and products, anchored to vehicle registration and vehicle parc data, so that product, strategy, and sales teams can benchmark competitors, size markets, and track adoption trends against a consistent taxonomy. Our coverage supports use cases from competitive benchmarking and market sizing to sales enablement and investment guidance for teams operating in fleet telematics.

The role

We are recruiting experienced freelance telephone interviewers to conduct voice of customer primary research interviews with senior executives and industry experts in the automotive industry in September 2026. Interviews will be run on our CATI system, covering France, Switzerland, Germany, Austria, and Poland. This is high-caliber B2B research, not consumer polling: respondents are hard-to-reach professionals, so credibility, business fluency, and the ability to hold a real conversation on the topic matter as much as script delivery.

Tasks

  • Conduct telephone interviews with executives and experts using our CATI platform
  • Recruit and schedule respondents within target quotas
  • Probe and follow up naturally within a semi-structured guide, without straying from the research objectives
  • Accurately log responses and flag data quality issues
  • Meet weekly interview completion targets

Requirements

Native or near-native fluency in French, German, or Polish (please specify your language(s) when applying), with strong working English for briefings and reporting

Proven experience conducting qualitative and quantitative B2B or executive-level telephone interviews (market research, CATI, or expert network background strongly preferred)

Comfortable engaging senior professionals (C-suite, engineers, fleet/procurement managers) and adapting tone accordingly

Familiarity with, or genuine interest in, the automotive/connected mobility sector is a plus

Available for a defined number of interview hours per day, with flexibility across time zones (France, Switzerland, Germany, Austria, Poland)

Benefits

Freelance/project-based contract, fully remote

Competitive day rate, commensurate with language and seniority (details discussed at interview)

Ongoing project pipeline across multiple waves of connected mobility research

Clear briefing, scripts, and support from the PAVE Insight research team

This is an opportunity for a freelancer to collaborate on a project basis from a remote location, with working hours split across French, German, Polish, and Swiss/Austrian business hours as needed for each market.

It is PAVE Insight's policy that there shall be no discrimination on the grounds of gender, race, ethnic origin, marital status, religious belief, sexual orientation, disability, age, nationality or national origin in any matters to do with employment.

If you feel like this is an opportunity for you, please send your CV, relevant language(s), a short note on your B2B/executive interviewing experience, and your day rate expectations before August 15th, 2026

About Mass Culture

Mass Culture is a growth media agency. We help mission-driven scale-ups connect brand and performance so they grow faster, more profitably, and with purpose.

About the Role

Mass Culture treats paid media as a single, orchestrated growth system, not a set of channels running in isolation. The Director, Media Planning owns the architecture behind that system: the cross-channel plan that connects paid social, paid search, CTV, retail media, and emerging platforms to a client's real business goals, margins, and growth stage.

This is a strategy-first role focused on planning and optimizing media execution. You will build the media plans clients act on, defend the logic behind budget allocation across channels, and make sure up-funnel and down-funnel investment work together instead of competing for the same dollar. You will stay close enough to the campaigns themselves to know when a plan needs to change, and why, and you will be the one to change it.

You will say what you expect each dollar to do before you spend it, define in advance what would make you move it, and come back to every allocation decision to say whether it worked. That is a higher bar than most agencies hold themselves to, and it is why clients trust us with the whole mix instead of one channel.

You will plan inside a proprietary platform. Channel budgets and line items, monthly pacing, KPI targets, market splits, and a surplus ledger that records the rationale behind every dollar that moves. You will co-own the planning surfaces of that product alongside agency leadership. What a plan should capture, and what we should be able to model before committing a budget.

Responsibilities:

Media Strategy & Planning

  • Build full-funnel, cross-channel media plans that tie budget allocation, channel mix, and pacing directly to each client's revenue, margin, and growth targets.
  • Define the role each channel plays in the plan, whether that is reach, demand capture, retention, or proof, before arguing its number.
  • Own the media mix model for assigned accounts: determine how up-funnel investment (CTV, paid social awareness, emerging platforms) and down-funnel investment (paid search, retargeting, retail media) should work together, and adjust as performance and market conditions shift.
  • Translate client business objectives into measurable media plans, KPIs, and testing roadmaps.
  • Lead media planning sessions with clients, presenting the strategic rationale behind channel and budget decisions, not just the numbers.

The Allocation Argument

  • Set reallocation triggers up front: the conditions under which money moves, agreed in collaboration with the client.
  • Defend the plan without inflating it. Say what we don't know. And call out risks and assumptions.
  • Hold the up-funnel line. The hardest budget to defend is the one that doesn't convert this week. Build that case in advance, with evidence from the analytics team.
  • Grade our own allocations. Revisit every significant allocation decision against what actually happened, and say plainly when we got it right and when we got it wrong.

Cross-Channel Orchestration

  • Partner with channel leads across paid social, paid search, CTV, and retail media to ensure each channel's execution ladders up to one plan.
  • Identify where channels are working against each other, where budget is misallocated, and where a mixed media stack would reduce risk and capture more attention.
  • Use the agency's forecasting and planning models to show clients how channels interact, not just how each performs on its own.

In-Flight Budget Management

  • Own budget pacing across assigned accounts. Know where every account stands against plan, and act before a month closes badly rather than explaining it afterward.
  • Own reallocation end to end. When a channel underdelivers, you decide where the money goes, and the rationale gets written down at the moment of the decision.
  • Maintain the surplus ledger for your accounts: what moved, from where, to where, and why.

Measurement Partnership

  • Define the business questions worth testing and commission the work from the analytics team: incrementality tests, geo experiments, holdouts, and media mix experiments.
  • Turn measurement findings into budget decisions. A test that changes no allocation was either the wrong test or the wrong response.
  • Work to the agency's measurement standards rather than a parallel set. One definition of a metric, agency-wide.

Client Leadership

  • Serve as a senior strategic voice in client conversations, leading planning sessions and budget reviews with clarity and a clear point of view.
  • Partner with Account Strategists in QBRs, owning the media plan and the investment narrative while they own the relationship.
  • Translate performance data into business recommendations focused on revenue, margin, and efficiency, not platform vanity metrics.
  • Act as an escalation point for planning and strategy questions on assigned accounts.

Platform & Product Partnership

  • Co-own the planning surfaces of the Mass Culture client portal with agency leadership: what a media plan captures, how reallocation is recorded, and what we should be able to model before committing a budget.
  • Build in the platform directly. You will construct plans, pacing views, and budget structures yourself rather than handing a spreadsheet to someone else.

Team & Growth

  • Plan our most complex accounts personally, and build and lead the planning team behind them as the book grows.
  • Set the standard for what a Mass Culture media plan looks like, and coach strategists and channel leads to it.
  • Contribute media planning expertise to new business pitches and client onboarding.

Tools, Automation & AI

  • Use media mix modeling, forecasting, and reporting tools to build plans grounded in data, not instinct.
  • Incorporate AI tools into planning and analysis workflows to sharpen forecasting and surface patterns faster. AI should make good planners better, not replace their judgment.
  • Stay current on new platforms, ad formats, and measurement approaches, and bring what's relevant to clients before they ask.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • 10+ years of media planning or cross-channel strategy experience, ideally within a performance-driven or growth marketing agency.
  • Proven ability to build media plans that connect budget allocation across paid social, paid search, CTV, and other channels to business outcomes, not just channel-level KPIs.
  • Experience planning and managing budgets from small test allocations through multi-million-dollar annual books.
  • Strong command of media mix modeling, incrementality testing, and cross-channel attribution. Enough to commission the right test and interrogate the result, whether or not you run it yourself.
  • Fluency in direct-response economics: CAC, LTV, contribution margin, and the difference between blended and incremental efficiency.
  • Track record leading senior client conversations and defending strategic recommendations under scrutiny.
  • A plan you got wrong, and what you changed because of it. We will ask.
  • Practical experience incorporating AI tools into planning, forecasting, or analytical workflows.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to connect media strategy to revenue and margin.
  • Agency environment experience required.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with retail media platforms (Amazon, Walmart Connect, Instacart Ads) as part of a broader media mix.
  • Experience building or specifying planning and forecasting tools rather than only using them.
  • Experience managing or mentoring media planners.

Why Mass Culture

We are not a traditional agency. We work inside our clients' businesses, connect media strategy to real commercial outcomes, and treat growth as a system. Our sister company, Brains, is a world-class branding agency, and that relationship is real. We love brand as much as we love performance.

No hacking. No smoke and mirrors. Real growth.

Inside Sales Representative (Part Time Seasonal, Remote)

Storage Scholars is a high-growth company that’s undergone 100% year-over-year growth since its inception in 2017. Our goal is to change the way college students across the country move in and out of residence halls with our all-inclusive moving, storage and shipping service. Storage Scholars is fast-moving, tenacious, innovative, and core-product-focused. We strive to be the premium option among the competition by offering the best user experience available, which is dependent on continuously improving our technology. We expect passion and buy-in from every team member, no matter the role. We believe everyone, regardless of their position, brings unique knowledge, skills, and perspective that makes us who we are. All voices are not just welcomed but encouraged to be a part of the decisions and direction of the organization. At Storage Scholars, egos are left at the door, wins are celebrated as a team, and learning never stops.

As an Inside Sales Representative (Part Time Seasonal) at Storage Scholars, your primary responsibility is being a consultative guide for customers seeking solutions for student move-in, move-out, storage, and shipping. As a member of the greater Customer Experience Team, you will be a crucial link between the customer and their understanding and adoption of the services that we offer.

What you’ll do:

  • Field inbound leads from both lead form submissions and inbound calls.
  • Make proactive phone calls to existing and former customers to promote service usage.
  • Provide service estimates for customers via call, SMS, and email.
  • Guide customers through their order flow in our online portal to book their moves.
  • Promote additional services and service upgrades to customers, as well as generate referrals.

Required:

  • Exceptional communication with strong sales aptitude.
  • Strong critical thinking skills.
  • Ability to handle fast-paced changes and intense workloads.
  • Strong phone presence.
  • High emotional intelligence to understand fellow team members and clients alike.
  • Technologically savvy, with the ability to learn new software rapidly.

Preferred:

  • 1–2 years of customer-facing experience (such as retail, hospitality, or customer service).

Scope:

  • Part time, seasonal role: 15–25 hours/week on average, up to 40 hours/week during March - May.
  • The ability to work a flexible schedule on evenings and weekends as necessary during our peak season (March - September).
  • Preferred Start Date: 1/25/27
  • Contract End Date: 9/13/27

Compensation:

  • Estimated seasonal earnings: $4,500 – $10,000+
  • $Base pay plus per-customer commission. Earnings depend on hours worked (15–25 hrs/week) and monthly sales performance.

Other Benefits:

  • Fully Remote
  • Ability to grow with our rapidly growing company and team.

Location:

  • Remote

How Our Core Service Works:

Customers sign up on our web portal to schedule services on their respective campuses. Packing supply kits are shipped out to students as requested. The student packs their items, uploads a few photos to our portal, selects their desired insurance, locks it in their room, and can leave at will. Thanks to our partnership with the university, our staff comes in once the campus is vacant and moves all of the student belongings into a storage facility for the summer. Headline

Manage and review enquiries and complaints for the final ombudsman-style stage of a new standardised process for complaints about how safeguarding concerns have been handled by Church of England bodies. Handle enquiries and complaints in a fair, independent and timely manner, helping to deliver a high-quality complaints handling service and improve organisational learning.

Description

The Church of England’s Safeguarding Structures Reform Programme is delivering a programme to strengthen safeguarding and rebuild trust. The Programme will roll out a standardised process across Church of England bodies for complaints about how safeguarding matters have been handled. Where matters cannot be resolved locally, they can be referred to an independent complaints body to review and make a final determination.

The Complaints Reviewer is responsible for reviewing complaints and enquiries, carrying out investigations, gathering and assessing evidence, and making recommendations to the Independent Complaints Adjudicator. The role supports effective, transparent and empathetic complaint handling while contributing to service improvement and stakeholder confidence.

The postholder will work closely with the Independent Complaints Adjudicator, colleagues and external stakeholders, balancing casework delivery with continuous improvement and the promotion of best practice in complaints handling. The Complaints Reviewer may be delegated additional responsibilities by the Independent Complaints Adjudicator as relevant.

Responsibilities

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Managing a caseload of enquiries and complaints and ensuring that they are progressed in a timely manner.
  • Planning and conducting investigations, including gathering evidence, analysing information and seeking specialist advice where required.
  • Supporting the handling of subject access requests and other information rights enquiries relating to complaints and case records, including identifying, reviewing and providing relevant information in accordance with legal and organisational requirements.
  • Communicating effectively with complainants and stakeholders, managing expectations and providing clear written decisions and recommendations.
  • Maintaining accurate case records and using case management systems effectively.
  • Contributing to service improvement and best practice.
  • Supporting outreach activities and stakeholder engagement.
  • Building constructive working relationships.
  • Contributing to organisational objectives and policy development where appropriate.

Requirements

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Complaint handling, investigation or casework experience.
  • Strong analytical and evidence-assessment skills.
  • Excellent written and oral communication and report writing abilities.
  • Sound judgement, impartiality and discretion.
  • Strong organisational and prioritisation skills.
  • Experience using case management systems.
  • Stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
  • Commitment to continuous improvement, equality and inclusion.

Desirable

  • Experience supporting complaint handling, investigations, regulatory, safeguarding or ombudsman services.
  • Understanding of complaint handling principles and customer service standards.
  • Experience of applying trauma-informed principles in practice.
  • Experience working in a public sector, charity, regulatory or ecclesiastical environment.

jobs.description:
Principal Data Scientist, AI (Architect-Level Scope)

About KLDiscovery

KLDiscovery is a global eDiscovery and legal technology provider serving large law firms, corporate legal departments, and government agencies. We build and operate the products and services that legal teams rely on to manage, process, and review case data at scale. With operations across multiple countries and a client base that includes AmLaw 200 firms, we handle some of the largest and most complex matters in the industry.

About the Role

We're hiring our most senior AI practitioner — someone with genuine data science rigor who also wants to build. In this role, you'll set the scientific and architectural direction for gen AI and ML at KLDiscovery: designing the evaluation methodology that proves our AI holds up under legal scrutiny, choosing and validating the models and retrieval systems that power our products, and building the hardest parts of that system yourself.

This is one of the most interesting data science problem sets in enterprise software. You'll work with terabytes of real-world legal data — emails, contracts, chat transcripts, images, video, depositions, and regulatory filings — from some of the largest litigation and investigation matters in the world. The work is hard in ways that matter: documents are messy and adversarial, the stakes are real (privilege, defensibility, attorney work product), and getting the evaluation wrong has real consequences. AI that can surface key people, themes, and timelines in hours instead of weeks, or pre-classify millions of documents for relevance and privilege with results that survive scrutiny, directly changes the economics of how legal matters get resolved. We build solutions that turn data into evidence the legal system can trust.

This is a builder-first role, not a research-only or advisory one. You'll design experiments and evaluation frameworks that prove our AI is defensible in court, build the retrieval and agent systems that reason over case data, and personally ship the hardest, most novel parts of that system. You'll set strategic direction across Nebula, our eDiscovery platform, and CS & Operations, then prove out the science and the architecture by building it yourself. Not a role for anyone stepping back from the keyboard, and not a role for anyone who treats evaluation as an afterthought.

We offer competitive total compensation that includes base pay, bonus potential, equity, inclusive benefits, wellness programs, and perks. We use market and industry data to inform pay decisions while considering geography and labor markets, individual experience, and business needs. Individual compensation will vary, although a reasonable estimate of the current annualized base pay range for this position is $190,000 to $240,000.

Job location: Remote (candidate must be based in the United States)

Key Responsibilities

Own the science and the architecture, and build both personally. Design the experimentation and evaluation methodology that determines whether our AI's outputs are accurate, consistent, and defensible — then define the end-to-end gen AI architecture across Nebula and CS & Operations to deliver on it: LLMs, agent harnesses, RAG, vector search, embeddings, and model selection and triage. Build the hardest parts personally: prototype agent loops, design and run the evaluations that validate them, tune retrieval, and ship the shared infrastructure that powers AI Case Explorer (case overviews, timelines, key people and themes, PII surfacing, and Agent chat), AI Agent Review (pre-classifying relevance, privilege, and key issues, shipping MLP), and CS & Ops tech-enablement as part of our central work orchestration system.

Own evaluation rigor, AI/MLOps, and telemetry end-to-end. Design the statistical and experimental methodology behind our evaluation harnesses — the standard our outputs have to meet to hold up under legal scrutiny — and own the infrastructure that enforces it: model deployment and versioning, eval pipelines, drift and quality monitoring, cost and latency telemetry, and prompt and agent observability. Define and implement how we select, triage, and route across models (Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, open-source, fine-tuned), manage vector databases and retrieval, and evolve our evaluation methodology and agent harness as the frontier moves.

Lead the practice from the front. Set the technical and scientific bar by building, not by reviewing. Partner with Engineering, Product, and Data Science leadership to translate that rigor into shipped product. Raise the bar on both AI engineering and evaluation discipline, mentor senior ICs through hands-on technical leadership, build and maintain relationships with model and infrastructure vendors, and represent KLD's AI strategy directly with customers, partners, and at industry events.

What You Bring (Required)

  • 7+ years in data science, applied AI/ML, or ML engineering, with recent hands-on experience as a senior or principal-level practitioner in the gen AI era
  • Real training in statistics, experimentation, or applied research you know how to design an evaluation that actually tests what you think it tests, not just one that looks reasonable
  • Proven track record architecting and personally building enterprise gen AI systems in production with measurable customer impact
  • Experience with consumer-facing or B2B customer-facing AI products — systems that real external users or customers depend on, not only internal tooling
  • Builder at heart: still writes code, runs experiments, ships, and tunes prompts and evals, and wants to keep doing so as a leader
  • Deep expertise across the modern gen AI stack: LLMs, agents, RAG, vector databases, embeddings, search, and evaluation harnesses
  • Hands-on experience designing system-of-systems AI pipelines spanning search, retrieval, agent harnesses, and model selection/triage

  • Supporting student onboarding sessions, in-class activities, demonstrations or peer Q&As
  • Creating social media content about Cengage products, student activities and your experience as an Ambassador
  • Writing student-focused content about your experience of digital learning
  • Creating a short video or testimonial about your experience with Cengage
  • Sharing authentic feedback and student perspectives with our team
  • Supporting selected Cengage marketing or student engagement activities
  • Attending training sessions and programme check-ins with the Cengage team

You won't be expected to know everything from day one. We'll provide training and guidance to help you understand our products, plan your activities and make the most of the programme.


Who are we looking for?

You don't need extensive work experience. We're much more interested in your enthusiasm, ideas and ability to connect with other students.


You'll be a great fit if you:

  • Are currently enrolled as an undergraduate, postgraduate or PhD student
  • Study at an institution using a relevant Cengage digital learning product
  • Are a confident and friendly communicator
  • Enjoy helping and engaging with other students
  • Are organised, reliable and comfortable managing your own time
  • Can work independently and meet agreed deadlines
  • Are interested in creating content or using social media
  • Are comfortable getting involved in student-facing activities

Experience with social media, video creation, presenting, student societies, peer support or campus activities would be useful, but isn't essential.


What you'll get

As a Cengage Student Ambassador, you'll gain practical experience that you can add to your CV and talk about in future interviews, including:

  • Working with a global education and technology company
  • Marketing and social media experience
  • Content and video creation
  • Presentation and communication skills
  • Student engagement and peer support
  • Experience managing your own activities and deadlines
  • The opportunity to share the student voice directly with Cengage

Most importantly, you'll play a role in helping fellow students get more from the digital learning tools designed to support their studies.


How does the programme work?

The programme is designed to fit around your studies. Rather than working fixed weekly hours, you'll complete a series of agreed activities and can organise much of the work around your own schedule.


Depending on your location and programme length, the expected commitment will be approximately 26 hours over a six-month programme or 37 hours over a nine-month/full programme.


You'll also attend three online training sessions and a programme check-in, giving you support and guidance throughout your time as an Ambassador.


Payment

This is a paid opportunity.


Depending on programme length and location, Ambassadors will receive:

£350 (or local equivalent) for the shorter/pro-rated programme, or
£500 (or local equivalent) for the full programme.


Payments will be made in stages during the programme, subject to completion of the agreed activities.


About Cengage

Cengage is a global education technology company helping millions of learners develop the skills and knowledge they need to achieve their goals.

As a Cengage Student Ambassador, you'll help us make sure our digital learning products don't just reach universities – they genuinely reach, engage and support the students they're designed for.


Interested? We'd love to hear from you.

Apply to become a Cengage Student Ambassador and turn your student experience into experience that can help shape your future career.

Company Overview

At FUJIFILM Healthcare Americas Corporation, we’re on a mission to innovate for a healthier world, and we need passionate, driven people like you to help us get there. Our cutting-edge healthcare solutions span diagnostic imaging, enterprise imaging, endoscopic and surgical imaging, as well as in-vitro diagnostics.

But we don’t stop at healthcare; our Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) team harnesses advanced radiography solutions to keep transportation infrastructure, aerospace, and oil and gas assets safe and running smoothly.

Ready to innovate, collaborate, and make a difference? Join us and bring your big ideas to life while working in a dynamic, flexible environment that fuels your creativity and drive.

Our headquarters is in Lexington, Massachusetts, an inspiring healthcare research hub in a historic town.

Fujifilm is globally headquartered in Tokyo with over 70,000 employees across four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging. We are guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles.” Visit:

Job Description

Duties and responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain the third-party support strategy for the Medical Informatics product portfolio.
  • Partner with product management and operational teams to assess vendor support needs, customer impact, lifecycle status, risk, and cost.
  • Lead or support vendor discussions and negotiations covering service scope, renewals, pricing, replacement services, and escalation expectations.
  • Review vendor proposals and agreements to identify coverage gaps, unclear responsibilities, unfavorable limitations, and customer-impact risks.
  • Maintain support entitlements, lifecycle information, vendor scorecards, risk registers, renewal forecasts, and leadership reporting.
  • Monitor vendor responsiveness and performance, support escalations, and recommend corrective actions or support-level changes.
  • Align third-party support capabilities with customer commitments and advise stakeholders on what can responsibly be offered.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce unnecessary spend, standardize third-party support tiers, consolidate services, and improve third-party support processes.
  • Develop and maintain the enterprise strategy for third-party support arrangements across the Medical Informatics product portfolio.
  • Partner with Product Management and operational stakeholders to understand how third-party products and services enable customer deployments and service offerings.
  • Recommend the appropriate third-party support level based on customer impact, operational and contractual risk, lifecycle status, replacement needs, service expectations, and cost.
  • Advise leadership on the business and customer implications of unsupported, under-supported, obsolete, end-of-life, or otherwise high-risk third-party offerings.

  • Working understanding of enterprise technology, clinical software, hardware, integrations, and product lifecycle concepts.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, documentation, communication, and negotiation skills.

  • Experience creating entitlement matrices, vendor scorecards, risk registers, dashboards, or executive reporting is preferred.

  • The ability to use your hands and fingers to feel and manipulate items, including keyboards, up to 100% of applicable work time.
  • The ability to stand, talk, and listen for 75% of applicable work time.

INDG creates digital twins and CGI content systems for global product brands. In our Automotive vertical, that means turning complex vehicle data into images and animations that can represent a car across configurators, launch campaigns, print, exhibitions, and promotional videos.

We are looking for a Senior 3D Artist who can turn complex automotive data into polished visual output. You will work from high-poly vehicle assets, build materials, render stills and animations, composite final images, and keep quality consistent across large content sets.

Your impact is visible. You will create content that represents premium automotive brands in configurators, campaigns, launch campaigns, retail tools, and large-format experiences. The work must look beautiful, but it also has to survive scale.

What You Will Do

  • Create automotive CGI that holds up at close range
    Build still images and animations from high-poly vehicle models. Texture, shade, light, render, and composite final content for automotive brands with strict visual standards. You will work on exteriors, interiors, detail crops, accessories, colorways, wheels, trims, and motion sequences.

  • Own the render, not just the task
    Evaluate image quality from a senior production perspective. You can see when a render issue comes from lighting, material response, geometry, camera setup, render settings, or compositing. You will refine clearcoat, metallic flakes, glass, rubber, leather, stitching, displays, brushed metal, chrome, and shadow behavior until the image feels physically and visually right.

  • Work inside scalable production pipelines
    Create scenes and outputs that can survive large content sets. You will follow naming, versioning, render-layer, compositing, and scene-organization standards. You will help keep assets clean, reusable, and ready for configurators, campaign derivatives, market adaptations, and automated content workflows.

  • Improve quality while delivering content
    Implement feedback from art directors, leads, clients, and production teams without losing control of the setup. You will spot recurring issues, improve material libraries, refine lighting templates, document useful fixes, and help reduce manual rework across automotive production.

Requirements

You Have

  • Strong experience in automotive CGI and high-end 3D production. You are comfortable working with complex high-poly models, physically based materials, lighting setups, render passes, compositing workflows, and final image polish.

  • You know 3ds Max, V-Ray, Photoshop, and Nuke or After Effects at a professional level. Your portfolio or showreel demonstrates seniority through visual judgment, technical control, and finished output, not just clean modeling or isolated shots.

  • You can communicate clearly in English with artists, leads, producers, and technical teams. You can explain what is wrong in an image, what needs to change, and what tradeoff is being made.

Why Join INDG

INDG has spent more than 20 years building visual production systems for global brands. We are not a traditional creative agency and not a pure software vendor. We build the systems that turn physical products into digital twins, production-grade CGI, and scalable content.

Grip extends that work into AI-assisted content orchestration. For a Senior 3D Artist, that means your craft does not disappear into automation. It defines the quality standard the system must reproduce.

jobs.excerpt: The OpportunityFutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to leadRiuso, an AI recommerce venture.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to leadRiuso, an AI recommerce venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Riusois the operating record for electronics returns and liquidation benches. Owner-operated resellers and refurbishers spend around eleven minutes identifying, grading and pricing each returned or liquidated unit by hand. When the bench backs up, units default to the liquidation pallet, the lowest-value exit.Riusoidentifies and grades each unit from photos in seconds and prices every disposition route, from resell and refurb to part-out, wholesale and pallet. It then routes the unit to the highest-recovery option. Every decision becomes memory the bench owns: repeat models price instantly, seller manifest accuracy builds over time, and outbound IMEI records turn mismatched returns into winnable claims. It runs on a phone and a label printer, with no integration.

Market Context

US consumers returned an estimated $849.9B of merchandise in 2025, and North American refurbished electronics is a roughly $17B market growing at double digits. Riuso addresses a $2.2B TAM across North American returns and recommerce benches. Its beachhead is 12,000 electronics-focused owner-operators, a $144M SAM. Right-to-repair laws now in force across California, New York, Texas, Oregon and five other states are deepening the parts market. Tariffs on new devices are pulling more buyers toward refurbished. Both make every unit on the bench worth more to price correctly.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven venture building team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

  • Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception

  • Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding

  • Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one

  • Investor and advisor network across supply chain tech and early-stage capital markets

  • A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight’s cross-functional team as your partner

What You’ll Own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead execution.

  • Strategy — Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning

  • Customer Development — Lead pilots with owner-operated electronics resellers and refurbishers, convert them to paid engagements, and build the go-to-market motion

  • Product — Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback

  • Capital — Lead the seed raise, supported by FutureSight's network and traction

  • Team — Recruit and lead the founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

Co-Founder Profile

  • Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company

  • Demonstrated success in B2B SaaS go-to-market, including sales and customer engagement

  • Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital

  • Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent

  • Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company

  • Direct exposure to electronics resale, liquidation, refurbishment or reverse logistics

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

jobs.excerpt: This role is fully remote, open to candidates based anywhere in the United States outside New York.
jobs.description:
This role is fully remote, open to candidates based anywhere in the United States outside New York. Based in New York? Apply to the New York posting of this role instead.

A Different Kind Of Job Description

At Filed, we believe in radical transparency. Everything is open: company finances, team salaries, stock options, anonymous team feedback. That extends to how we talk about this job, so what you'll read here looks a little different from other job ads. It starts with why this is a terrible job. Then it explains why it might be the best career move you'll ever make.

Why this is a terrible job

This is an incredibly high-paced, high-tempo environment. We're making a generational bet to change all of our lives, and generational bets are not comfortable.

You will stop signing returns. There are no clients of your own here, no book to build, no partner track. If the thing you want is the next rung on a firm ladder, this job takes it away from you on day one.

You will be on calls most of the day. You carry 5 to 10 firms at a time through onboarding and you own whether they actually succeed, for 8 weeks each, with your name attached. When a firm is floundering in week six, that is yours to fix, and there is nowhere in this job to hide from it.

The calendar is not negotiable. Firms will not change their stack mid-season, so December and January are relentless and everything has to land before the February 1 freeze. Miss the window and you wait a year.

Tax law is objective, but what applies under it and how professionals interpret it is full of judgment. You can give two tax professionals the same task and get two different results where both are right. You will sit across from a partner who disagrees with what the system did, and you will have to explain it in their language, without hiding behind the software. At times it will feel like hitting your head against the wall.

Customers will sometimes get frustrated, because they expect deterministic results from probabilistic systems, and we're managing the expectations of some of the biggest firms in the world, including the Big Four. You will be the person in the room who has actually done their job, which means the hard calls land with you.

And the rhythm is real. It's tough. It's relentless.

Why it might be the best career choice you'll ever make

You already know how to win a room full of sceptical tax professionals, because you have been one. Here that is the whole job, and it compounds: every firm you bring through onboarding properly becomes a firm that stays, refers, and grows.

It's addictive to be part of a business when you know you're winning. Filed is adding millions of dollars of revenue every quarter, and in under two years we've become the market leader in a space with entrenched incumbents and a drastic need for new AI tools. When we come into head-to-heads with competitors, we win every time, because our product is superior.

The industry looks boring from the outside, but the problem is unsolved, and the space has been riddled with products below the mark for decades. When you push through the wall, there's a spark of joy: a customer says "wow, this is phenomenal." That keeps happening, and you will be the one in the room when it does.

The opportunity here is not only to make a great deal of money. It's to have real impact on our mission: making this profession extraordinary. Nobody became a tax professional for the admin. They got into this work to be creative with tax law, to have fun, and to change the fabric of society. Filed enables them to do exactly that.

We've raised $17.2 million to date, led by Northzone. Our focus now is to deliver the roadmap and continue to win.

What You'll Own

As a Member of Accounting Staff, you own the moment a firm goes from signed to genuinely working:

  • The technical demo on customer calls, where you show firms what Filed does and why it answers the problem you have lived yourself

  • Group onboarding, 5 to 10 firms at a time, from kickoff to the point where the firm is running real work through Filed without you

  • The relationship through the 8 weeks that decide whether a firm succeeds or quietly churns

  • The feedback loop back into product, so the friction you watch firms hit gets fixed rather than repeated

You'll see your decisions carry real weight for some of the most demanding professional users in the world within days, not quarters.

What You'll Be Responsible For

  • Running the technical demo alongside sales on firms that need a tax professional in the room

  • Onboarding firms in groups and staying their point person until they are genuinely winning, backed by customer support

  • Teaching: webinars, training sessions, and the ongoing work of making firms good at Filed

  • Translating between firms and engineering, so what you hear on calls turns into what gets built

  • Knowing the product well enough to be trusted on it, including catching output that would not pass a reviewer

Your Hard Skillset

  • You have prepared or reviewed real returns inside a real firm. Credentials are welcome but not required, what matters is that you've done the work

  • Real strength in either individual returns (1040) or business returns (1065, 1120, 1120-S, 990, 1041), enough that a partner takes you seriously in the first five minutes. One or the other is enough. Strength in both is a plus

  • You are comfortable in front of customers. Demos, training, difficult conversations, escalations

  • A high degree of confidence in a few of the major tax platforms, such as CCH Axcess, UltraTax, Lacerte, ProConnect, Drake, or GoSystem. Nobody is expert in all of them, and we don't expect you to be

  • You pick up software fast. A product surface, a new workflow, an integration conversation, none of it puts you off

  • Bonus if you've been through a SurePrep, GruntWorx, or AutoFlow implementation, or rolled new software out across a firm

Your Soft Skillset

  • Comfortable being uncomfortable and making calls with incomplete data

  • Empathetic and curious: building for the user, not just for the technically correct answer

  • Highly collaborative across product, engineering, and tax

  • Detail-oriented but pragmatic: you know when precision matters and when to move

  • You own your work and welcome the accountability that comes with it

A championship team

We think of ourselves as a sports team. Incredibly high performance, incredibly high standards, and real success to show for it. Being a championship team means working with people who are deeply proud of the work they do and have great fun doing it together.

We measure employee happiness constantly, and our eNPS is +60. We don't say that to brag. We say it because a team playing at this tempo only holds together if people genuinely love being on it. Every four months, the whole company comes together for an offsite.

What Filed Stands For

Not posters. Not corporate language. Real operating standards.

No problem is someone else's problem. If you see it, it's yours. Bugs, customer confusion, missed expectations, internal friction. We don't pass problems sideways and we don't hide behind roles. You fix the typo even if you didn't write it, jump into a customer issue even if it's not your department, escalate early, and close loops fully. Ownership means you drive resolution, not that you suffer silently or burn out doing everything alone.

Waiting is not a strategy. Momentum is our advantage. We don't wait for perfect information or stall because something is unclear. You ship a V1 instead of debating V5, test instead of theorize, run small experiments instead of requesting big approvals, and propose solutions instead of just naming blockers. Speed is powerful. Sloppiness is not, and recklessness has no place in a high-trust industry.

We run toward the fire. When something breaks, we move. Tax is high-stakes and trust is fragile. We acknowledge issues immediately, communicate clearly and often, prioritize customer-impacting problems fast, and stay on it until it's fully resolved. Firefighting is a strength, not panic, and never an excuse for preventable mistakes.

We win on customer experience. AI will commoditize. Features will copy. Pricing will compress. Experience won't. We respond faster than customers expect, communicate proactively, think like a partner rather than a ticketing system, and anticipate needs before they're raised. Overdelivering means raising the standard of care, not overpromising, hero culture, or burning the team out.

Who This Suits

This is a very fun environment, but it only suits people who meet the criteria we're looking for:

  • People who want to win

  • People who have a point to prove

  • People who want to write their own job descriptions

How We Pay

Nothing at Filed is behind closed doors. Everyone here sees everyone else's salary, because we believe transparency creates trust, and trust is the foundation of excellent teamwork. Compensation isn't a negotiation. Depending on your location, everyone receives the same three offers, and all of our offers are above market benchmarking.

This role is assessed at Level 3. The salary and equity bandings are:

  • Most Equity: $85,800 per year + $130,027 of equity

  • Great Equity: $93,600 per year + $86,684 of equity

  • Good Equity: $101,400 per year + $43,342 of equity

We run performance reviews every four months. Meet your goals and you can expect to double your equity by the end of your first year.

One more thing, in the spirit of transparency: some people who apply for this role will be assessed at a different level. If the team determines your level of responsibility sits differently, we'll adjust the offer accordingly.

Benefits

  • Platinum-level medical insurance, fully covered for you, with 100% coverage for your dependents as well

  • Dental insurance

  • Vision insurance

  • 401(k) retirement plan

  • Paid maternity and paternity leave

  • A minimum of 30 days of paid holiday every year

  • Your choice of the latest and greatest computers, plus a budget for your home office setup

  • Company-wide offsites every four months

The process

  • Quick intro call (30 minutes)

  • Product walkthrough and async exercise (60 minutes)

  • Final round with our team (60 minutes)

In just 2.5 hours, you'll be wanting early access, just like the rest of our team, to get into the product and start building a generational company, even before your first day.

About Filed

Filed is the AI tax preparer trusted by America's accounting firms.

Taxes might seem boring, but they are the $5 trillion backbone of the US economy. Globally, nearly $15 trillion in taxes is collected every year. Behind every dollar of it sits a professional making judgment calls, and the industry that does this work is breaking under a talent shortage no one has solved. We're fixing it. Firms run Filed inside the systems they already use, and we're backed by Northzone, Neo, Analog, and Raine.

There has never been a more exciting time to work on a problem this complex. Join us while "I was there when it all started" is still true.

Performance matters. We take pride in it. We own it. We show up for one another and for our communities.

Because at Driven Brands, we're not just fixing cars. We're building futures, unlocking potential, and fueling what's possible — together.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Senior Lead - Consumer Insights will help shape how Driven Brands understands, serves, and grows with consumers across its portfolio of automotive aftermarket brands. This role will translate consumer feedback, research findings, and market signals into actionable insights that inform brand strategy, customer experience improvements, marketing decisions, and operational priorities across the enterprise.

Reporting to the Vice President of Marketing Data Analytics, this role will partner closely with Marketing, Operations, Customer Experience, Strategy, Brand, and Product stakeholders to design research, synthesize findings, and deliver clear recommendations that drive measurable business impact. This is a hands-on, mid-level role ideal for an insights professional with at least 5 years of experience turning focus groups, surveys, customer feedback, and behavioral data into practical actions for business teams.

Responsibilities

  • Transform business questions into customer research initiatives by identifying the right research approach, right questions, and right vendors to provide the voice of the consumer to the business.
  • Translate consumer feedback from focus groups, surveys, reviews, social listening, customer support interactions, and other listening channels into actionable insights and business recommendations across the Driven Brands portfolio
  • Partner with Marketing, Operations, Customer Experience, Brand, Product, and Strategy teams to define research questions, identify learning objectives, and connect insights to enterprise and brand-level decisions
  • Lead and support primary consumer research initiatives, including survey design, discussion guide development, vendor coordination, fieldwork management, and results synthesis
  • Analyze qualitative and quantitative research findings to identify consumer needs, pain points, motivations, purchase drivers, loyalty drivers, and opportunities to improve experiences across brands and service categories
  • Develop clear, compelling insight narratives and presentations that convert research findings into practical recommendations for leadership and cross-functional partners
  • Monitor consumer trends, competitive activity, brand perceptions, and category dynamics to inform growth opportunities, positioning, and customer engagement strategies
  • Support measurement of customer experience and marketing initiatives by connecting consumer feedback to operational, brand, and business performance outcomes
  • Maintain organized research documentation, insight repositories, and recurring reporting that make consumer learning accessible and usable across the organization
  • Oversee brand health surveys including brand awareness and ad effectiveness to help guide brands on the health of their brand with the consumer.
  • Serve as a trusted consumer advocate by ensuring customer perspectives are represented in planning, prioritization, and decision-making discussions across Driven Brands

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Psychology, Sociology, Statistics, Market Research, or a related field
  • 5+ years of experience in consumer insights, market research, customer experience research, brand strategy research, or a related insights function
  • Experience translating consumer feedback from focus groups, surveys, interviews, customer reviews, or similar sources into actionable business recommendations
  • Strong understanding of qualitative and quantitative research methods, including survey design, segmentation, concept testing, customer journey research, brand tracking, and thematic analysis
  • Ability to synthesize complex information into clear insight stories, executive-ready presentations, and practical recommendations for both enterprise and brand-level audiences
  • Experience working with research vendors, managing project timelines, and ensuring research outputs meet business objectives
  • Strong analytical skills with comfort interpreting survey data, customer feedback trends, competitive research, and behavioral or transactional data
  • Proficiency with Excel and PowerPoint; experience with survey platforms, data visualization tools, or statistical analysis tools preferred
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders through consumer-led storytelling
  • Self-motivated, organized, and comfortable managing multiple research priorities in a fast-paced, multi-brand environment

Are you a former law firm attorney with a passion for technology and innovation?

This could be the opportunity for you.

You'll act as a trusted adviser to senior legal stakeholders, combining your understanding of legal practice with innovative technology to design, develop and implement tailored workflows that deliver real business value.

You'll also have the opportunity to influence future product development, ensuring client feedback and practical legal experience help shape the next generation of legal AI solutions.

  • Source and qualify opportunities based on growth potential, brand strength, and strategic fit

  • Assumes account ownership from the Program Director, Consumer Health, at the completion of customer onboarding, and coordinates with that role on service escalations

  • Bachelor’s degree

About the role

The Executive Director, Consumer Health Partnerships is responsible for driving the development and execution of partnerships and client relationships that expand the reach and impact of direct-to-consumer (DTC) diagnostic testing. This leader will identify, evaluate, and scale partnerships with digital health companies, telehealth platforms, health systems, and emerging consumer health players.

Coverage spans the full range of commercial relationships, from strategic partnerships through standard client and sales relationships. Not every account in scope will be structured as a strategic partnership.

This role is accountable for prospecting new opportunities and establishing high value partnerships that extend Labcorp’s diagnostic capabilities into evolving consumer care models. The Executive Director will position Labcorp as a preferred partner in digital first healthcare ecosystems, enabling broader access to diagnostics beyond traditional care channels.

The role carries full ownership of partnerships with DTC players (e.g., wearables, wellness companies, and digital health platforms) and operates in a shared ownership model with Divisions, National Accounts, and IT for enterprise relationships (e.g., health systems, national physician groups, and technology companies).

Scope distinguishes three relationship types: partners whose consumer offering Labcorp enables in the partner environment, partners that order through Labcorp OnDemand, and partners embedded in Labcorp consumer channels.
