jobs.title: Technical Co-founder (CTO) - AI Workforce for Solo Practitioners and Small Law F
jobs.excerpt: The OpportunityAI is changing the economics of legal practice.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

AI is changing the economics of legal practice. Work that once took hours can increasingly be done in minutes, creating both enormous leverage for lawyers and new pressure to win and serve more clients efficiently.

Yet solo practitioners and small law firms still face many of the same constraints: missed calls, slow follow-up, intake handled between client matters, inconsistent marketing, and administrative work competing with billable time. Building larger intake, administrative, and marketing teams is expensive and increasingly unnecessary.

BloomLex is building a different model: a managed AI workforce that helps small law firms grow without growing their team.

The customer thesis has been validated through live pilots, and multiple deployments are moving into production evaluation. The next phase is proving in-production reliability, delivery economics, repeatability, and scalability. The companies that successfully deploy trusted AI workers into professional-service verticals over the next 18 months have an opportunity to define entirely new categories. We intend to be one of them.

The Venture

BloomLex is building an AI workforce for solo practitioners and small law firms, helping them win and serve more clients without adding headcount.

We call the broader shift the Rise of the Solo: AI gives an individual lawyer or a small firm access to capabilities that historically required a much larger organization.

Unlike self-serve software, BloomLex is fully managed. We configure, deploy, monitor, and continuously improve the AI workforce for each firm. Our customers evaluate us on outcomes — calls answered, prospective clients captured, consultations booked, demand generated, follow-up completed, and time saved — not on how much software they configure themselves.

Our Bloomlex workforce starts with two teammates:

Ava — AI Front Desk. Ava answers calls 24/7, handles structured intake, screens and routes inquiries, books consultations, performs outbound callbacks and follow-up, and integrates those interactions into the firm's workflow.

Claire — AI Marketing Assistant. Claire helps firms generate and nurture demand through content, digital marketing, campaign management and optimization, lead nurturing, and ongoing marketing execution.

Together, Ava and Claire address both sides of growth: Claire helps create demand; Ava helps ensure that demand is captured and converted.

They are also the beginning, not the end, of the platform. Our roadmap expands the AI workforce across the operational side of the practice — including custom workflows and additional specialized AI roles — all delivered through the same managed model and coordinated around the lawyer.

The Partnership

The CEO co-founder is in place. The customer thesis is validated, design partners are engaged, live pilots are running, and the initial product architecture exists. What remains is to bring on the technical co-founder — a partner who will own product and engineering with the same conviction, urgency, and ownership as the CEO.

This is a co-founder role, not a CTO hire. In return for that level of commitment, you receive founder-level equity, founder-level authority with decision collaboration on product, technology, hiring, fundraising, and strategy, and a genuine partnership with the CEO on every material decision.

You will inherit working products and live deployments, but you will not inherit sacred architecture. Your job is to determine what should survive, what should be rebuilt, and what needs to exist for BloomLex to scale from pilots to thousands of firms.

Role & Responsibilities

As Co-Founder & CTO, you will be a hands-on builder first and the architect of the technical organization that follows.

  • Product & Architecture — Own the technical architecture across Ava, Claire, and the broader BloomLex AI workforce. Make the build-versus-buy decisions that determine where BloomLex creates durable technical advantage.

  • Voice AI & Reliability — Harden Ava's real-time voice, telephony, intake, scheduling, routing, and workflow systems for production reliability. Establish observability, evaluation, escalation, and audit-trail standards appropriate for a trust-sensitive environment.

  • Agentic Workflows — Build reliable AI systems capable of executing multi-step operational and marketing workflows across voice, email, SMS, web, calendars, CRM and practice-management systems, with appropriate human oversight.

  • Managed AI Delivery Layer — Build the internal infrastructure that allows BloomLex to configure, deploy, monitor, evaluate, and continuously improve AI workers across hundreds and eventually thousands of firms without scaling engineering or implementation headcount linearly.

  • AI Quality & Economics — Own the trade-offs among model capability, latency, reliability, privacy, and inference cost. Build an architecture capable of delivering strong gross margins within the initial ~$499/month product model as usage scales.

  • Data, Security & Trust — Establish the security, privacy, tenancy, permissions, data-retention, and audit architecture required to earn the trust of law firms and their clients.

  • Customer & Market — Work directly with lawyers and design partners, translating real-world workflows and failure modes into product decisions. Represent BloomLex with customers, partners, and investors as the technical voice of the company.

  • Roadmap — Help convert pilots into repeatable commercial deployments, expand the AI workforce beyond Ava and Claire, deepen integrations into law-firm workflows, and establish a path toward custom and self-hosted models where economics, performance, privacy, or legal requirements justify them.

  • Team — Recruit and lead the founding engineering team and establish a culture of speed, accountability, technical rigour, and customer obsession.

Co-Founder Profile

We are looking for a technical founder, not simply an engineering manager.

You have:

  • Shipped LLM-powered, agentic, voice, or automation systems into production environments where incorrect outputs and system failures carried meaningful consequences

  • Full-stack confidence across applied LLMs, conversational and real-time voice AI, APIs and integrations, workflow orchestration, observability, data architecture, and secure multi-tenant SaaS

  • Strong instincts around AI evaluation, reliability engineering, edge-case management, hallucination mitigation, human-in-the-loop design, and production monitoring

  • Well-formed convictions about the trade-offs among AI quality, latency, reliability, privacy, and cost

  • Experience building platforms that combine software with managed or service-heavy delivery, with the discipline to automate delivery rather than scale headcount linearly

  • The ability and willingness to work directly with customers and turn messy real-world workflows into reliable products

  • The mindset of a principal and owner — including the willingness to say “this won't scale,” “this isn't ready,” or “we need to rebuild this” when the integrity of the product requires it

  • The desire to remain deeply hands-on while building the team around you

Strongly preferred:

  • Prior founder or early-stage technical leadership experience

  • Experience with production voice AI, telephony, agentic workflows, or AI evaluation infrastructure

  • Background in legal tech, healthcare, financial services, or another trust-sensitive vertical

  • Experience with security, privacy, and compliance requirements involving sensitive customer data

  • Experience deploying or self-hosting open-source/custom models where privacy, latency, control, or economics require it

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

Our group brings together three European software brands that help organisations earn and use data with trust: Cookie Information for consent management; Piwik PRO for privacy-by-design analytics and data activation; and Sheltr for reliably finding personal data in internal data sources.

Headquartered in Copenhagen with an office in Wrocław, our team of 180 people have been building trusted data solutions since 2011. We work with companies and marketing teams across various industries that take control of their data model, including some of the most data-sensitive clients in healthcare, finance, energy & utilities, and the public sector. We are proud that our clients rely on us to meet GDPR and EU data residency requirements across EMEA and the US, as this regulatory depth is hard to build and replicate. We believe compliance and performance are not opposites. Consented data, auditable analytics and full visibility of personal data belong to one data journey; together they form a foundation that marketing, IT, legal and the C-level can rely on.

Our journey is to move from a regulation-driven house of brands to one unified company with a clear point of view. jobs.description:
This role is fully remote, open to candidates based anywhere in the United States outside New York. Based in New York? Apply to the New York posting of this role instead.

A Different Kind Of Job Description

At Filed, we believe in radical transparency. Everything is open: company finances, team salaries, stock options, anonymous team feedback. That extends to how we talk about this job, so what you'll read here looks a little different from other job ads. It starts with why this is a terrible job. Then it explains why it might be the best career move you'll ever make.

Why this is a terrible job

This is an incredibly high-paced, high-tempo environment. We're making a generational bet to change all of our lives, and generational bets are not comfortable.

You will stop signing returns. There are no clients of your own here, no book to build, no partner track. If the thing you want is the next rung on a firm ladder, this job takes it away from you on day one.

You will be on calls most of the day. You carry 5 to 10 firms at a time through onboarding and you own whether they actually succeed, for 8 weeks each, with your name attached. When a firm is floundering in week six, that is yours to fix, and there is nowhere in this job to hide from it.

The calendar is not negotiable. Firms will not change their stack mid-season, so December and January are relentless and everything has to land before the February 1 freeze. Miss the window and you wait a year.

Tax law is objective, but what applies under it and how professionals interpret it is full of judgment. You can give two tax professionals the same task and get two different results where both are right. You will sit across from a partner who disagrees with what the system did, and you will have to explain it in their language, without hiding behind the software. At times it will feel like hitting your head against the wall.

Customers will sometimes get frustrated, because they expect deterministic results from probabilistic systems, and we're managing the expectations of some of the biggest firms in the world, including the Big Four. You will be the person in the room who has actually done their job, which means the hard calls land with you.

And the rhythm is real. It's tough. It's relentless.

Why it might be the best career choice you'll ever make

You already know how to win a room full of sceptical tax professionals, because you have been one. Here that is the whole job, and it compounds: every firm you bring through onboarding properly becomes a firm that stays, refers, and grows.

It's addictive to be part of a business when you know you're winning. Filed is adding millions of dollars of revenue every quarter, and in under two years we've become the market leader in a space with entrenched incumbents and a drastic need for new AI tools. When we come into head-to-heads with competitors, we win every time, because our product is superior.

The industry looks boring from the outside, but the problem is unsolved, and the space has been riddled with products below the mark for decades. When you push through the wall, there's a spark of joy: a customer says "wow, this is phenomenal." That keeps happening, and you will be the one in the room when it does.

The opportunity here is not only to make a great deal of money. It's to have real impact on our mission: making this profession extraordinary. Nobody became a tax professional for the admin. They got into this work to be creative with tax law, to have fun, and to change the fabric of society. Filed enables them to do exactly that.

We've raised $17.2 million to date, led by Northzone. Our focus now is to deliver the roadmap and continue to win.

What You'll Own

As a Tax Product Specialist, you own the moment a firm goes from signed to genuinely working:

  • The technical demo on customer calls, where you show firms what Filed does and why it answers the problem you have lived yourself

  • Group onboarding, 5 to 10 firms at a time, from kickoff to the point where the firm is running real work through Filed without you

  • The relationship through the 8 weeks that decide whether a firm succeeds or quietly churns

  • The feedback loop back into product, so the friction you watch firms hit gets fixed rather than repeated

You'll see your decisions carry real weight for some of the most demanding professional users in the world within days, not quarters.

What You'll Be Responsible For

  • Running the technical demo alongside sales on firms that need a tax professional in the room

  • Onboarding firms in groups and staying their point person until they are genuinely winning, backed by customer support

  • Teaching: webinars, training sessions, and the ongoing work of making firms good at Filed

  • Translating between firms and engineering, so what you hear on calls turns into what gets built

  • Knowing the product well enough to be trusted on it, including catching output that would not pass a reviewer

Your Hard Skillset

  • You have prepared or reviewed real returns inside a real firm. Credentials are welcome but not required, what matters is that you've done the work

  • Real strength in either individual returns (1040) or business returns (1065, 1120, 1120-S, 990, 1041), enough that a partner takes you seriously in the first five minutes. One or the other is enough. Strength in both is a plus

  • You are comfortable in front of customers. Demos, training, difficult conversations, escalations

  • A high degree of confidence in a few of the major tax platforms, such as CCH Axcess, UltraTax, Lacerte, ProConnect, Drake, or GoSystem. Nobody is expert in all of them, and we don't expect you to be

  • You pick up software fast. A product surface, a new workflow, an integration conversation, none of it puts you off

  • Bonus if you've been through a SurePrep, GruntWorx, or AutoFlow implementation, or rolled new software out across a firm

Your Soft Skillset

  • Comfortable being uncomfortable and making calls with incomplete data

  • Empathetic and curious: building for the user, not just for the technically correct answer

  • Highly collaborative across product, engineering, and tax

  • Detail-oriented but pragmatic: you know when precision matters and when to move

  • You own your work and welcome the accountability that comes with it

A championship team

We think of ourselves as a sports team. Incredibly high performance, incredibly high standards, and real success to show for it. Being a championship team means working with people who are deeply proud of the work they do and have great fun doing it together.

We measure employee happiness constantly, and our eNPS is +60. We don't say that to brag. We say it because a team playing at this tempo only holds together if people genuinely love being on it. Every four months, the whole company comes together for an offsite.

What Filed Stands For

Not posters. Not corporate language. Real operating standards.

No problem is someone else's problem. If you see it, it's yours. Bugs, customer confusion, missed expectations, internal friction. We don't pass problems sideways and we don't hide behind roles. You fix the typo even if you didn't write it, jump into a customer issue even if it's not your department, escalate early, and close loops fully. Ownership means you drive resolution, not that you suffer silently or burn out doing everything alone.

Waiting is not a strategy. Momentum is our advantage. We don't wait for perfect information or stall because something is unclear. You ship a V1 instead of debating V5, test instead of theorize, run small experiments instead of requesting big approvals, and propose solutions instead of just naming blockers. Speed is powerful. Sloppiness is not, and recklessness has no place in a high-trust industry.

We run toward the fire. When something breaks, we move. Tax is high-stakes and trust is fragile. We acknowledge issues immediately, communicate clearly and often, prioritize customer-impacting problems fast, and stay on it until it's fully resolved. Firefighting is a strength, not panic, and never an excuse for preventable mistakes.

We win on customer experience. AI will commoditize. Features will copy. Pricing will compress. Experience won't. We respond faster than customers expect, communicate proactively, think like a partner rather than a ticketing system, and anticipate needs before they're raised. Overdelivering means raising the standard of care, not overpromising, hero culture, or burning the team out.

Who This Suits

This is a very fun environment, but it only suits people who meet the criteria we're looking for:

  • People who want to win

  • People who have a point to prove

  • People who want to write their own job descriptions

How We Pay

Nothing at Filed is behind closed doors. Everyone here sees everyone else's salary, because we believe transparency creates trust, and trust is the foundation of excellent teamwork. Compensation isn't a negotiation. Depending on your location, everyone receives the same three offers, and all of our offers are above market benchmarking.

This role is assessed at Level 3. The salary and equity bandings are:

  • Most Equity: $85,800 per year + $130,027 of equity

  • Great Equity: $93,600 per year + $86,684 of equity

  • Good Equity: $101,400 per year + $43,342 of equity

We run performance reviews every four months. Meet your goals and you can expect to double your equity by the end of your first year.

One more thing, in the spirit of transparency: some people who apply for this role will be assessed at a different level. If the team determines your level of responsibility sits differently, we'll adjust the offer accordingly.

Benefits

  • Platinum-level medical insurance, fully covered for you, with 100% coverage for your dependents as well

  • Dental insurance

  • Vision insurance

  • 401(k) retirement plan

  • Paid maternity and paternity leave

  • A minimum of 30 days of paid holiday every year

  • Your choice of the latest and greatest computers, plus a budget for your home office setup

  • Company-wide offsites every four months

The process

  • Quick intro call (30 minutes)

  • Product walkthrough and async exercise (60 minutes)

  • Final round with our team (60 minutes)

In just 2.5 hours, you'll be wanting early access, just like the rest of our team, to get into the product and start building a generational company, even before your first day.

About Filed

Filed is the AI tax preparer trusted by America's accounting firms.

Taxes might seem boring, but they are the $5 trillion backbone of the US economy. Globally, nearly $15 trillion in taxes is collected every year. Behind every dollar of it sits a professional making judgment calls, and the industry that does this work is breaking under a talent shortage no one has solved. We're fixing it. Firms run Filed inside the systems they already use, and we're backed by Northzone, Neo, Analog, and Raine.

There has never been a more exciting time to work on a problem this complex. Join us while "I was there when it all started" is still true.

Job Title:  Manager, Assessment Development Reports to: Director, Assessment Development Department: Assessment Solutions Location:  Remote with some Travel About the Role: The Assessment Development Manager (ADM) leads and manages a team of Assessment Development Specialists responsible for developing and maintaining certification, licensure, and K-12 assessment programs. In addition to providing leadership and oversight for team operations, the ADM directly supports assigned assessment programs and clients through assessment development activities, consultation, and program management. This role is responsible for developing team capability, managing workload and resources, ensuring quality and consistency of deliverables, and supporting the successful delivery of assessment programs. The ADM collaborates closely with psychometricians, subject matter experts, clients, and cross-functional teams to ensure assessments meet industry standards, psychometric requirements, and client expectations. Responsibilities: Leadership & Team Management

Lead, coach, and mentor team members, supporting professional growth and development.

Oversee recruitment, onboarding, training, and performance management activities.

Establish performance expectations and provide ongoing feedback, coaching, and development opportunities.

Assign, prioritize, and monitor work across team members to ensure timely delivery of assessment development services.

Monitor team workload and capacity, balancing resources to meet project and client needs.

Foster a collaborative, accountable, and inclusive team environment.

Support employee development, knowledge sharing, and succession planning efforts. Promote consistent application of assessment development standards, processes, and best practices across the team.

Assessment Development Operations & Collaboration

Provide oversight of assessment development activities, including blueprint development, item development and review, item banking, form assembly, test maintenance, and related assessment development processes.

Serve as a primary assessment development contact for assigned clients and programs, providing consultation and support throughout the assessment development lifecycle.

Ensure assessments align with approved specifications, psychometric requirements, industry standards, and client expectations.

Establish and monitor quality control measures to promote consistency, accuracy, validity, and fairness of assessment content.

Support the development, implementation, and improvement of assessment development processes, procedures, and best practices.

Collaborate with psychometrics, publishing, PMO, account management, and other stakeholders to support successful delivery of assessment programs.

Facilitate or support assessment development workshops and related activities, including item writing, item review, and form review meetings, as needed.

Communicate project status, risks, resource needs, and assessment development updates to leadership and stakeholders.

Support accreditation, compliance, and audit activities related to assessment programs.

Qualifications: Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in education, measurement, psychology, a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Five or more years of experience in assessment development, certification/licensure, educational measurement, K-12 assessment, or a related field.

Demonstrated leadership, supervisory, or project leadership experience.

Knowledge of assessment development practices, psychometric principles, and industry standards.

Strong communication, organizational, problem-solving, and relationship management skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading remote or geographically distributed teams.

Experience supporting multiple assessment markets or audiences, such as certification, licensure, K-12, higher education, or workforce credentialing.

Familiarity with assessment technologies, item banking systems, test assembly tools, or test delivery platforms.

Exposure to multiple assessment models, including fixed-form, adaptive, LOFT, performance-based, or other assessment approaches.

Demonstrated success implementing process improvements, quality initiatives, or operational efficiencies.

Additional Information:

Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends as needed.

Travel may be required (up to 20%).

  • Proficient programming experience in Go, Java, Python or similar object-oriented languages.
  • Experience operating large-scale, distributed systems on top of cloud infrastructure.

Location

This role will be based in any of the permitted 5 India states (Delhi, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana & TamilNadu)

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

Job Title: Senior Clinical Data Manager- Oncology- Remote, Canada

Job Overview:

  • Data Management leadership on studies and take responsibility for the development of the project documentation, system set-up, data entry and data validation procedures and processes assigned to more junior staff. Assume responsibility for all DM activities (from study start-up to database lock) according to client quality expectations, within project timelines and budgets. Act as subject matter expert (SME) for DM activities in relationship meetings with Sponsors. Work directly with Sponsors to understand their direct requirements and lead implementation of those requirements. Regularly review client specific process to ensure they remain optimal for Sponsor and Fortrea. The Senior Clinical Data Manager will work with the leadership team to provide guidance, mentoring and training to DM to ensure best working practices are maintained.

Summary of Responsibilities:

  • Lead studies including (but not limited to) a combination of healthy volunteer and patient populations, multi-site, complex protocol design, strong client management required or reduced timelines. Ability to organize and effectively prioritize workload and deliverables.
  • As the Study Manager, be accountable for all DM deliverables as assigned per the established timeline; providing instruction to their DM study team(s) and review of their study team’s output to ensure the highest quality, while adjusting resource allocations accordingly.
  • Ensure that all allocated projects are carried out in strict accordance with the relevant protocols, global harmonized SOPs, and the specified standards of GCPs.
  • Work with the Project Manager(s) or FSP Lead (or designee) to build timelines to meet contracted milestones by communicating with leads in different disciplines and the full project team as necessary, including at study initiation meetings.
  • Provide DM project team leadership and accountability; leads data focused internal project team meetings; meets frequently with the study leads of EDC Design, SAS Programming, Statistics, and PK to ensure that all deliverables are planned and coordinated intradepartmental; proactively identifies potential risks/mitigations, effectively communicates data-driven discussions in order to achieve database lock dates; keeps the Project Manager or FSP Lead (or designee) apprised of project progress.
  • Maintain awareness of other Biometrics functional group deliverables to be able to support risk and mitigation strategies, including impact on DM resources or deliverables and consult with Project Manager (or designee) and/or functional group management as necessary.
  • Keep Project Manager (or designee), Biometrics management team and/or sponsor services informed of pertinent project or sponsor related information (i.e., budget status, work scope changes, timeline impacts).
  • Coordinates the receipt and inventory of all data related information, from clinical sites and vendors as appropriate to meet timelines for deliverables. Ensure all appropriate documentation and procedures are performed upon project completion.
  • Develop and maintain client relationships and review client satisfaction surveys. Implement appropriate action plans including driving process improvements and team training.
  • Track scope changes and work with the Project Manager or FSP Lead (or designee) to ensure that Sponsor approval is received, and the scope change processed.
  • Provides leadership, mentorship, and coaching in DM related clinical trial processes, department technical capabilities, and associated turnaround durations to the internal study team.
  • Provide support to DM supervisors and managers on the performance evaluation of other team members, provide constructive feedback to aid in career development, interpersonal skills, and achievement of competency standards.
  • Accountable for learning new DM technologies and applied processes, keeping up to date with industry wide technology and feasibility for process improvement at Fortrea.
  • Ensures service and quality meet agreed upon specifications per the DMP and scope of work.
  • Have input in writing, reviewing, and updating SOPs and associated documents as required.
  • Maintain accurate records of all work undertaken.
  • Perform reconciliation of the clinical database against safety data, laboratory data or any other third-party data as appropriate. Utilize local laboratory systems and batch data load facilities where appropriate.
  • Represent DM and where necessary overall Biometrics in new business opportunities.
  • Attend and action client or internal audits as appropriate and resolve all issues within an appropriate timeframe. Address client comments with the study team.
  • Works with management team to develop and implement directional strategy by providing technical input into discussions and rolling out training/mentorship to DM staff (as required).
  • Actively promote Biometrics services to sponsors whenever possible.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned by management.
  • All other duties as needed or assigned.

Qualifications (Minimum Required):

  • University / college degree.
  • Experience and/or education plus relevant work experience, equating to a bachelor's degree will be accepted in lieu of a bachelor’s degree.
  • Fortrea may consider relevant and equivalent experience in lieu of educational requirements.
  • Language Skills Required:
  • Speaking/Writing/Reading: English required.

Experience (Minimum Required):

  • 3-5 years of Oncology experience is required
  • Thorough knowledge of clinical trial process, DM, clinical operations, biometrics, and system applications to support operations.

jobs.description:
Why Work at Mercer Advisors?

For more than 40 years, Mercer Advisors has been helping families amplify and simplify their financial lives by integrating financial planning, investment management, business management, tax, estate, insurance, and more, all managed by a single team. We deliver the kind of comprehensive care once reserved for only the wealthiest households.

Today, we serve over 42,800+ families across 110+ cities across the U.S. Ranked the #1 RIA Firm in the nation by Barron’s for two consecutive years, Mercer Advisors is an independent fiduciary legally bound to act in our clients’ best interests — always.*

Mercer Advisors offers a workplace that stands apart in the financial industry. More than half of our employees and client-facing professionals are women, reflecting the clients we serve. With a flexible, national footprint, we build our teams around exceptional talent — wherever they are.

Join us and help families amplify and simplify their financial lives with confidence.

* Mercer Advisors was ranked #1 for RIA firms with up to $70 billion in assets. The Barron’s top RIA ranking is based on a combination of metrics – including size, growth, service quality, technology, succession planning and others. No fee was paid for participation in the ranking, however, Mercer Advisors has paid a fee to Barron’s to use the ranking in marketing. Please see important information about the ranking criteria methodology here.

Job Summary:

At Mercer Advisors, our purpose is to amplify and simplify our clients’ financial lives through a fully integrated family office offering. We bring together fiduciary professionals across disciplines to do the best work of their careers—as one unified team committed to doing what’s right for clients. We continue to reinvest in our people and platform so that our growth creates more opportunities for teammates and more value for clients.

Regis is Mercer Advisors’ offer designed for ultra-high net worth families with complex, multi-generational wealth. Regis clients often have the means to build their own family office, and they require a deeply integrated wealth management experience with the highest level of service, coordination, and sophistication. We are a team of world-class fiduciary professionals delivering holistic advice across investments, financial planning, estate strategy, tax strategy, and more with the aim of making every client feel like our only client.

We are seeking an exceptional Tax Partner - Regis - to serve as the lead tax advisor, strategist, and subject matter expert for our Regis families. You will lead engagements alongside senior wealth advisors and other Regis team members, with direct accountability for the tax outcomes and experience of our most complex families. This is not a support or review role—you will bring the credibility, judgment, and gravitas that UHNW families expect from their most trusted advisors.

Essential Job Functions for this role include:

  • Serve as the lead tax advisor and primary point of accountability for a select group of Regis families, maintaining and growing a book of clients with balance sheets that often exceed +$100M.
  • Build practical, year-round, and multi-year tax strategies tailored to each family’s goals, ownership structures, businesses, trusts, investments, charitable activities, and succession plans.
  • Lead and develop a select team of UHNW-focused tax professionals supporting Regis engagements, overseeing staffing, engagement economics, billing, and service quality.
  • Identify planning opportunities and risks arising from business transactions, concentrated positions, real estate, carried interests, equity compensation, major charitable gifts, residency changes, and cross-border exposure (foreign trusts, PFICs, GILTI, FATCA/FBAR) bringing in specialists when the issue calls for deeper expertise.
  • Oversee tax compliance at a level appropriate to each engagement: directly, when Mercer prepares the returns, or through active review and coordination when a family’s own CPA firm or internal tax team handles preparation.
  • Lead the response to significant federal and state tax notices, examinations, and controversy matters, coordinating with counsel and other specialists through resolution.
  • Partners with Regis wealth advisors and Mercer’s broader team — estate planning, investments, financial planning, and family office services — so tax advice is fully integrated with each family’s overall plan.
  • When relevant, collaborate and coordinate the tax calendar / division of responsibilities with the families outside CPAs, attorneys, trustees, investment bankers, valuation professionals, controllers, and other advisors
  • Support new client development through prospective client meetings and partner with Regis leadership to evolve the tax service model, team, and technology.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • CPA license required; advanced degree in taxation (MST/LL.M.), law degree, or comparable technical credential strongly preferred.
  • 12–15+ years of progressive tax experience, with the majority spent advising clients with balance sheets of $25M or greater; meaningful experience with $100M+ families required.
  • Deep technical command of individual, fiduciary, partnership, corporate, estate, gift, and state and local taxation, including advanced planning strategies commonly used by ultra-high net worth families.
  • Experience identifying cross-border tax and reporting issues and working effectively with international tax specialists; direct technical expertise in every international area is not required.
  • Experience managing significant tax notices, examinations, and controversy matters, including coordination with tax counsel.
  • Meaningful experience advising entrepreneurs, business owners, executives, and multi-generational families through liquidity events, business succession, wealth transfer, and other significant transactions.
  • Ability to analyze complex facts, focus on what matters, and deliver clear, practical recommendations — with excellent written and verbal communication skills to explain sophisticated tax matters in plain language.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and develop high-performing tax professionals and build a culture of accountability and technical excellence.
  • Comfort operating in a team-based, integrated advisory environment within a regulated RIA structure; experience at a family office, multi-family office, wealth management firm, or national accounting firm strongly preferred.
  • Unquestioned integrity and a strong commitment to confidentiality, sound risk management, and putting the client’s interests first.
  • Ability to travel up to 10%.

Work Schedule:

This professional role requires availability during standard business hours of Monday through Friday from 8AM to 5PM. At times, the role may have early or late hours to meet business tasks and deadlines for external and internal client needs.

All roles classified as a non-exempt are required to record working time into the timekeeping system daily at the start and end of each workday plus a 30-minute unpaid lunch period.

Working Conditions:

This position may be in a professional office environment or a dedicated home office workspace which is free of interruptions. Whether position is in a dedicated office space or home office workspace, basic technology needs will be provided to satisfy position requirements. Routinely sitting and standing for periods of time. No heavy lifting over 10 lbs.

Application Deadline: The initial deadline for applications is 9/14/2026. Applications submitted after this date may still be considered on a rolling basis until the position/program is filled. We encourage all interested candidates to apply as early as possible. If a final decision has not been made by the initial deadline, subsequent applications will be reviewed as they are received.

The annualized compensation range for this role is based on factors including, but not limited to, experience, skillset, and geographic location where work is performed. The cash compensation range includes both base salary and an annual bonus. The total compensation package may include additional cash bonus amounts and other incentive compensation.

Total expected cash compensation range
$250,000—$400,000 USD

Benefits:

Mercer Advisors offers a competitive and robust benefit package to our employees. Our benefit programs are focused on meeting all of our employees and their eligible dependents health and welfare needs. We offer the following:

  • Company Paid Basic Life & AD&D Insurance
  • Company Paid Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Insurance
  • Supplemental Life Short-Term Disability; Accident; Critical Illness; and Hospital Indemnity Insurance
  • Three Cigna medical plans offerings including two High Deductible Health Plans and a Traditional Co-Pay medical plan.
  • Kaiser Medical plans available in California
  • Health Savings Account (HSA) with company contributions if enrolled in either HDHP medical plan.
  • Two comprehensive Dental Plans
  • Vision Insurance Plan
  • Dependent Care Savings Account for child and dependent care.
  • 14 Company Paid Holidays including a full week off at Thanksgiving.
  • Generous paid time off program for vacation and sick days
  • Employee Assistance Plan
  • Family Medical Leave
  • Paid Parental Leave (8 weeks)
  • Maternity benefits utilizing company paid STD, any supplemental STD, plus Parental Leave (8 weeks) to provide time for recovery, baby bonding, and enjoying your family time.
  • Adoption Assistance Reimbursement Program
  • Company Paid Concierge Services for you and your loved ones for the spectrum of caring needs for your aging parents, young children, life’s challenges and more.
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan with both Traditional and Roth plans with per pay period match as well as an after-tax option
  • Pet Insurance
  • Personalized financial planning and guidance from Mercer Advisors professionals, offered at preferred employee pricing

Today we support 14 FROs and counting across the US, the UK and Chile, with an annual budget of $75 million and growing. Large-scale brain mapping, climate measurement and software for math all have something in common: they each need a nonprofit legal entity, payroll providers, health benefits, boards, contracts, office space, press releases, websites… For every FRO we support, Convergent provides the backend infrastructure that lets them move fast.

About the Role

As the Controller, you oversee the full accounting operation across Convergent, its disregarded entities and its subsidiaries, from the general ledger and monthly close to internal controls, audit and regulatory compliance. You will also build and run our federal grants program: designing the compliance infrastructure, monitoring every award, and executing against 2 CFR Part 200 from award setup to closeout. Reporting to the Head of Finance, you will lead a team of Finance & Accounting Managers and serve as our in-house expert on GAAP and federal grant compliance, weighing in on matters of significance with team, FRO and Convergent leaders.

This is a fully remote position with domestic travel required quarterly for team and organizational onsites, and as needed.

You Are

  • A seasoned nonprofit accountant. You bring deep, hands-on experience across the full accounting cycle in nonprofits, including fund accounting, net asset restrictions, multi-entity consolidation, and revenue recognition for contributions, grants and exchange transactions. You enjoy solving complex reconciliation challenges and have a passion for financial accuracy.

  • The in-house GAAP expert. You support the Head of Finance in researching and documenting technical accounting positions, such as conditional grants, restricted gifts, leases and intercompany transactions, and leaders rely on your judgment on matters of significance.

  • Audit-seasoned. You have participated in more audits and single audits than you can count and have filed just as many 990s. You know what the auditors will ask before they ask it.

  • A federal grants program builder. You know all the components of 2 CFR Part 200. You have built federal grant compliance programs from the ground up: written the policies, procedures and control documentation, stood up the systems, and audited them yourself. You are comfortable across agencies and award types, including grants, cooperative agreements and other transactions.

  • A people leader. You have led accounting teams, including managers. You set clear standards, review work closely and help your team grow.

  • Pleasantly detail-obsessed. You sweat the details, but don’t get hung up on immaterial ones. You know when it’s appropriate to push back for compliance or GAAP sake.

  • Systems-savvy. You enjoy working with multiple systems and have a firm grasp of accounting systems. You know when to ask for systems help too!

  • A natural collaborator. You can translate a complex journal entry into plain English for a non-finance colleague without breaking a sweat.

You Will

  • Own the close. You oversee monthly reconciliation and close across Convergent, its disregarded entities and its subsidiaries, including consolidation and intercompany. You set the close calendar and review standards, and you know the ins and outs of every detail on those balance sheets.

  • Lead the accounting team. Manage and develop a team of Finance & Accounting Managers. Set priorities, review their work, and design metrics to measure performance and team successes.

  • Build the federal grants program. Design and implement Convergent’s federal grants compliance program under 2 CFR Part 200, including policies and procedures, internal controls, allowable cost review, time and effort reporting, cost allocation, indirect and fringe rate support, and subrecipient monitoring.

  • Oversee every award. Make sure the Finance & Accounting Managers manage each federal award across Convergent and its FROs correctly from award setup through closeout. Review their budget-to-actuals, burn rates, cost share, drawdowns and invoicing, federal financial reports, SEFA and procurement documentation such as debarment checks and sole-source justifications, and step in early when risks or errors surface.

  • Own audit readiness. Lead preparation for the annual audit and the Single Audit, including PBC requests, supporting schedules, SEFA and corrective action plans, coordinate 990 workpapers with our preparer, and own regulatory financial reporting.

  • Own revenue and restrictions. Make sure revenue recognition, donor restriction tracking and releases, payroll allocations and time and effort reporting are accurate across every entity.

  • Turn numbers into insight. As first line reviewer of monthly financial reports, you review monthly financials for relevancy, consistency, and completeness, and advocate for changes that make reports useful for decision-making.

  • Strengthen systems and controls. Write and maintain accounting SOPs and internal control documentation, improve workflows and systems, and keep controls tight across every entity.

  • Lead the in-house transition. Partner with the Head of Finance to move work from our outsourced accounting firm in-house, mapping each task to an owner and keeping the close on track during the handoff.

  • Partner on budgets and policy. Support the Head of Finance on the annual budget, financial policies and internal control design, and serve as backup on chart of accounts changes.

  • Bring the whole team along. You make financial insights accessible and actionable, whether you're talking to a scientist, an engineer, or a program lead.

In 6 months you will have (6 months goals)

  • Learned the business of each FRO and understood its accounting and grant needs.

  • Built strong relationships with your team, internal teams, FRO leaders, auditors and external accounting partners.

  • Assessed our federal grants compliance against 2 CFR Part 200, delivered a roadmap, and put the priority policies and controls in place.

  • Set up award-level monitoring for every active federal award.

  • Brought the monthly close onto a consistent calendar with clear review standards across your team.

We Offer (Amazing Benefits)

  • A rare chance to build institutional architecture for frontier science and work with some of the smartest and most talented experts from different fields

  • Competitive Salary: $176,000. Convergent uses a consistent compensation philosophy across all roles, and we offer a 5-10% premium for those working from especially high cost of labor locations (e.g. NYC, San Francisco) or from our NYC office. This structure helps us keep pay transparent, consistent, and equitable.

  • Up to a 6% 401k match because future-you deserves comfort

  • Top-tier medical, dental, and vision insurance—majority of options are fully covered for you and your dependents. Stay healthy, my friend

  • Company-paid life insurance, AD&D, long- and short-term disability insurance, as well as voluntary supplemental insurance options

  • 19 holidays (including a full week off at the end of the year—yes, we enforce it)

  • 3 weeks PTO with tenure increases, with separate allotments for sick and parental leave

  • Generous fertility benefits and childcare reimbursement—because tiny humans are a big deal

  • Education and professional development benefits

  • Wellness allowance for fitness and wellness activities (treat yourself to climbing shoes or Calm.com—no judgment)

  • 3x/year offsite team retreats and additional opportunities to meet your teammates in person

Convergent Research aims to help fill a structural gap in today's R&D system. We enable fundamental research that requires unusual levels of scale and coordination yet is not rapidly monetizable by industry. We’re bringing together top talent from academia, industry, and startups to build a new model for innovative R&D.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. We believe in hiring individuals based on their unique talents—not on race, color, religion, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law or our company policies. We are more than a proud Equal Employment Opportunity employer. Our goal is to foster a healthy, safe, and respectful environment where all employees are valued and treated with dignity. Harassment of any kind is not tolerated here.

Clovr Labs is recruiting a Software Engineer to work on new and interesting projects.
Let's give you some context on who we're looking for and what to expect when you join the team.
👋 About us

Clovr Labs is a boutique consulting firm working at the intersection of cybersecurity, Bitcoin, and lean product development. We care deeply about building simple, elegant solutions to complex problems and believe in iterating quickly to uncover the best ideas.

We’re developing a range of products across several cutting-edge technology domains, including Bitcoin and the Lightning Network, powering instant, low-cost payments at scale. One of our flagship products is, an enterprise-grade payment service provider built on the Lightning Network.

🧩 Your role

We’re looking for engineers who are curious, driven, and excited about creating high-quality software.

As a Payments Software Engineer at Clovr Labs, you will:

  • Help evolve and expand our existing products and internal systems.

  • Work closely with a motivated and collaborative team to build new automation and infrastructure solutions.

  • Design and deliver product features that bring real value to our clients.

  • Dive into the details, polish the experiences you build, and take pride in high craftsmanship.

🎬 What do we expect from you?

  • Business mindset: you understand the business goals behind your work and choose technology that serves those goals and delivers value for customers and the company. You seek user feedback and iterate quickly based on real-world insights.

  • Strong sense of ownership: you understand the problem, find or build the right solution, and take responsibility for delivering it to production and ensuring it works reliably.

  • Strong security mindset: you proactively assess risks, anticipate threats and failure scenarios, and design and code defensively to protect our customers.

  • Experience with production systems: you are comfortable operating live services and use logs, metrics, and traces to understand system behavior, detect issues early, and resolve them effectively.

  • Correctness and financial integrity: you design for idempotency, data consistency, and precise monetary calculations, handle retries, concurrency, and partial failures safely, ensuring every transaction is traceable and can be reconciled.

  • Adaptability: you stay committed and flexible as priorities change, adjusting your approach as new information emerges.

  • Teamwork makes the dream work: you are a strong team player and believe that a team together can ship great things. you work closely with others, challenge ideas respectfully, welcome being challenged, and take shared responsibility for the team’s success.

  • AI-powered engineering: you use AI as a core part of your workflow to understand problems, explore solutions, and accelerate delivery, applying engineering judgment to validate its output and taking ownership of the results.

  • English proficiency is helpful; understanding Spanish is a nice plus.

🛠 Key roles

  • You will join a small team currently scaling up. We are passionate about it and we are not trying to hide it.

  • We expect you to bring your experience in implementing best practices to our team such as pair programming, continuous deployment, tech debt management.

  • A key part of our duties is to dedicate time to non-business requirements of the systems we are working on, such as cost, maintainability, scalability, and security.

  • Self learning is an expectation. You will be provided with enough time and resources to learn new stuff and to become a better developer.

  • You should have a cost-benefit analysis mindset and use logical reasoning to address the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions.

🎏 It's nice to have

  • Have a technical interest in Blockchain concepts, specially Bitcoin and the Lightning Network. Also in payments processors and understanding how these systems operate in practice.

  • Special interest and high understanding of modern cloud-native software solutions, with special focus on observability, security and performance.

  • Experience building software applications with a combination of Go and C# or can easily adapt to using these languages.

  • Interest in Open Source Software (OSS), we highly value contributions to Open Source Software. Many of our main components are OSS, and we take pride in contributing back to other OSS projects.

🔍 What we offer

  • Fully and asynchronous remote work within Spain, independence, ownership and flexibility is what you can expect from our mindset.

  • Fair wages for people with attitude above all (60k - 80k negotiable).

  • Evolve in a stimulating and challenging environment.

  • Share and learn with a passionate and diverse team.

  • Work from home budget, choose what you need to create your dream home office, including internet and electricity.

  • Annual learning budget, learn a new programming language or go to a tech conference, if it is important for your career, it is important for us.

  • Fully paid team building activities three or four times a year, somewhere around the world.

Clovr Labs is incorporated in Spain and the team meets regularly in Barcelona. We speak English and Spanish, most of the time at the same time, but we would appreciate it if you could send us the contents of your application in English.

Key Responsibilities

Test Automation & Quality Engineering

  • Design, develop, and maintain automated UI, API, and integration tests for web and mobile banking applications.

Digital Banking & Credit Union Testing

Engineering & Delivery

  • Work within Agile delivery teams and contribute to sprint planning, refinement and acceptance criteria.

  • Provide clear quality metrics, defect reporting, and release-readiness assessments.

  • Help establish automated quality gates for AI-assisted software development.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of professional software testing or quality engineering experience.

  • 3+ years of hands-on test automation development.

  • Experience testing financial services, banking, credit union or other transaction-intensive applications.

  • Strong proficiency with at least one modern test automation framework such as Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, or Appium.

  • Programming or scripting experience with TypeScript, JavaScript, Java, C#, or Python.

  • Strong API testing skills using tools such as Postman, REST Assured or equivalent.

  • Experience testing REST APIs, authentication, authorization and system integrations.

  • Experience with SQL, data validation, and troubleshooting integration issues.

  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and tools such as Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions or Jenkins.

  • Strong understanding of SDLC, Agile delivery, defect management and risk-based testing.

  • Excellent communication skills and ability to collaborate directly with client stakeholders.

Highly Desirable Experience

  • Direct experience with Canadian credit unions or digital banking transformation programs.

  • Testing digital banking platforms such as VeriPark, Backbase, Central 1 Forge/MemberDirect, Intellect Design, Temenos, Lumin or eBankIT.

  • Integration testing with core banking systems, especially Fiserv DNA or CGI RFS360.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 90 days, you will be expected to:

Why Join Aequilibrium?

The project and the team

What else you should know:

Your role

Do we have a match?

  • Experience with DSLs or data translation engines: Prior work involving declarative domain-specific languages (DSLs), schema-to-schema mapping, or data-driven code generation.

  • Automated testing & CI/CD workflows: Experience with network test frameworks (e.g., PyTest, PTF, Scapy) and automated validation pipelines in enterprise environments.

More reasons to join us

  • Flexible working hours and approach to work: fully remotely, in the office or hybrid

  • Professional growth supported by internal training sessions and a training budget

  • Solid onboarding with a hands-on approach to give you an easy start

  • A great atmosphere among professionals who are passionate about their work

  • The ability to change the project you work on

Your Mission

We are seeking a Lead Unreal Engine Developer to take technical ownership of the architecture, development, integration, and final delivery of a complex Unreal Engine application for an immersive, interactive experience.

In this role, you will bridge creative development, technical art, third-party software development, and physical AV systems integration.

You will be responsible for maintaining the Technical Design Document, defining the application's technical architecture, coordinating development tasks, and ensuring that all software components integrate into a stable, optimized, and deployable application.

We are looking for a hands-on technical leader who can balance creative ambition with practical implementation, proactively identify technical risks, collaborate with cross-disciplinary teams, and make informed technical decisions throughout production.

Roles and Responsibilities

1. Technical Architecture & Documentation

  • Own, develop, and maintain the Technical Design Document (TDD).
  • Define application architecture, software dependencies, integration requirements, and technical workflows.
  • Establish development standards and best practices for C++, Blueprints, project organization, and source control.
  • Identify technical risks, performance constraints, and potential integration challenges early in development.
  • Document the final application architecture and deployment requirements for ongoing maintenance and support.

2. Unreal Engine Application Development & Delivery

  • Lead the development, integration, optimization, and delivery of the final Unreal Engine application.
  • Implement and maintain core application systems using C++ and Blueprints.

  • Review completed work to ensure consistency with the overall application architecture.
  • Communicate technical progress, risks, and integration requirements to project stakeholders.

4. AV Hardware Consultation & Integration

  • Collaborate with AV integrators and hardware vendors to ensure the Unreal application operates correctly within the specified hardware environment.
  • Consult on GPU/CPU requirements, rendering performance, display configurations, and system architecture.
  • Support integration with external hardware, display systems, and control interfaces.
  • Identify and resolve hardware/software compatibility and performance challenges.
  • Participate in system testing, commissioning, and deployment as needed.

5. Web Overlay & UI Integration

  • Coordinate with a third-party web development vendor responsible for creating web-based UI overlays.

  • Integrate web overlays into the Unreal application, ensuring reliable communication, rendering, and interaction.
  • Troubleshoot integration issues and collaborate with the vendor on performance and compatibility.

6. Technical Art & Real-Time Visual Integration

  • Troubleshoot rendering, shader, material, and Blueprint integration issues.

We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable.

Our stack is Python (FastAPI) on AWS, with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows.

Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD.

What You Will Do:

  • Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end.

  • Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails.

  • Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production.

  • Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality.

  • Drive the full software development lifecycle, translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans.

What We Are Looking For:

  • 5+ years building and operating production backend systems, with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end.

  • Deep fluency in your primary backend language, and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly.

  • Strong systems fundamentals — concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes — and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one.

  • Sound reasoning under ambiguity: you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change.

  • Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations, including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar).

Even Better:

jobs.description:
As a Staff Network Engineer at vCluster Labs, you aren't just configuring switches; you are building the automation logic that configures them. AI Clouds run on InfiniBand and high-speed Ethernet fabrics that most teams still wire up by hand, one customer at a time. You will build the automation that turns that fabric into repeatable provisioning logic. You start in a small R&D group alongside our CTO and grow into owning this area as it becomes a core part of our platform.

As a Staff Network Engineer, your role will include:

  • Fabric automation: You will design and build the systems that automatically provision and configure NVIDIA switches and InfiniBand fabrics, including integration with NVIDIA UFM. Manual, per-customer switch setup is the thing you are replacing.

  • Network config management and sync: You will build the control loop that keeps switch, VLAN, and VXLAN state consistent with what our platform intends, detects drift, and reconciles it safely in production.

  • NAT gateway and L4 load balancing: You will build the gateway and load balancing layer that tenant clusters depend on for connectivity, with failover designed in from day one rather than bolted on later.

  • Scale and failure engineering: You will define how our network layer behaves at large scale: BGP route table limits, convergence, failover, and what happens when a link, switch, or gateway dies under real AI workloads.

  • Customer Zero for AI networking: You will run your automation on real AI Cloud environments, bring back what breaks, and turn hard-won operational lessons into product behavior our customers never have to think about.

  • Technical direction: You will help decide what we build versus integrate with partner solutions, write the design and requirements docs, and set the standards for how networking works across vCluster products.

This role could be a fit for you if you bring:

  • You have built network automation, not just operated networks: You have shipped software that configures switches, routers, or load balancers programmatically, ideally as part of a product or internal platform other teams relied on.

  • NVIDIA networking experience: Hands-on work with NVIDIA UFM, NVIDIA Spectrum or Quantum switches, Cumulus Linux, or NVUE, including programming against their APIs.

  • Deep fabric fundamentals: Strong command of InfiniBand, VLAN, VXLAN and EVPN, and BGP, including how they behave and fail at production scale.

  • Production scale scars: You have run networks at real production scale, seen them break, and helped fix the root cause with automation rather than runbooks.

  • Software engineering ability: You write production code in Go or Python, use version control and code review as a matter of course, and think of network config as code.

Bonus points for:

  • AI networking depth: Experience tuning fabrics for GPU training or inference workloads, such as RoCEv2, congestion control, rail-optimized topologies, or Spectrum-X.

  • AI Cloud or hyperscaler background: You helped build network automation at a GPU cloud, hyperscaler, or large CDN.

  • Load balancer and gateway internals: Experience building L4 load balancers or NAT gateways, including with eBPF/XDP or DPDK.

  • Open source: Contributions to networking or Kubernetes projects such as SONiC, FRRouting, Cilium, or MetalLB.

About vCluster Labs

We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

Benefits

We offer the following benefits:

  • Competitive Salary: We offer a competitive compensation package, including equity.

  • Premium Insurance: Health, dental, vision, and life Insurance, including plans for you and eligible dependents (benefits vary depending on country).

  • Flexible Working Schedule: You have a doctor’s appointment or need to head to the supermarket to get groceries at 2pm? We won’t have an issue with that. To us, results matter more than clocking in and out at the same time every day.

  • Workplace Flexibility: We’re very flexible about where you work. We know things can change in life and we’re happy to adjust the work environment for you along the way.

Culture & Values

At vCluster Labs, we value and stand for:

  1. Make it Happen: We have a relentless bias for action and the grit to push through obstacles. We do whatever it takes to figure it out, put in the work, and ruthlessly prioritize the actions that drive measurable impact for the business.

  2. Own the Outcome: We understand that our responsibility doesn't end when a task is checked off; it ends when the value is delivered. We connect our daily individual actions to the broader success of the company and our customers.

  3. Create Wow: We measure success by the experience we generate, both inside and outside the company. For our customers, this means impressive speed and intuitive experiences. For our team, this means going the extra mile to support one another and to continuously drive each other to new heights.

  4. Open Source, Open Mind: We are actively contributing to and maintaining open-source projects. Internally, we foster meritocracy — the strongest ideas win, no matter who or where they come from.

  5. Build Tomorrow’s Standards, Intentionally: We don't just ship software; we define the state-of-the-art of tomorrow. We are fearless in tearing down old approaches to build something better, but we are disciplined in how we do it because we know our users rely on our technology to run mission-critical infrastructure platforms.
